articleTitle: Long time bounds for the periodic KP-II equation
abstract: We prove that the solutions of the periodic KP-II equation issued from data of size ε ≪ 1 remain of size ε for time scales of order ε<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>.

articleTitle: Kähler solvmanifolds
abstract: Compact Kähler solvmanifolds are classified up to biholomorphism. A proof of a conjecture of Benson and Gordon that completely solvable compact Kähler solvmanifolds are tori is deduced from this.

articleTitle: Stability of periodic peakons
abstract: The peakons are peaked traveling wave solutions of a nonlinear integrable equation modeling shallow water waves. We give a simple proof of their stability.

articleTitle: Uniform approximate functional equation for principal L-functions (Erratum)
A quadratic bound for the determinant and permanent problem
abstract: The determinantal complexity of a polynomial f is defined here as the minimal size of a matrix M with affine entries such that f = det M. This function gives a minoration of the more traditional size of an arithmetical formula. Consider the polynomial “permanent” perm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> of a d × d matrix with entries X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,j</inf>. A conjecture in complexity theory says that the determinantal complexity (dc) of perm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> should not be polynomial in d. In this article we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dc}{({\text{perm}}_d)}\geq d^2/2$</tex> , improving the previously known minoration, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt2d$</tex> . We also begin a systematic study of the function dc, and compute it for the homogeneous polynomials of degree 2.

articleTitle: A lower bound on the density of sphere packings via graph theory
abstract: Using graph-theoretic methods we give a new proof that for all sufficiently large n, there exist sphere packings in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> of density at least cn2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−n</sup> exceeding the classical Minkowski bound by a factor linear in n. This matches up to a constant the best known lower bound on the density of sphere packings due to Ball. However, our proof is very different from the earlier constructions of Minkowski, Hlawka, Rogers, and Ball. Moreover, this proof makes it possible to describe the points of such a packing with complexity exp(n log n), which is significantly lower than in the other approaches.

articleTitle: Annular noncrossing permutations and partitions, and second-order asymptotics for random matrices
abstract: We study the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{S}}_{\text{ann}-\text{nc}}{(p,q)}$</tex> of permutations of {1, …, p+q} which are noncrossing in an annulus with p points marked on its external circle and q points marked on its internal circle. We define <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{S}}_{\text{ann}-\text{nc}}{(p,q,q)}$</tex> algebraically by identifying the crossing patterns which can occur in an annulus. We prove the annular counterpart for a “geodesic condition” shown by Biane to characterize noncrossing permutations in a disc. We examine the relation between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{S}}_{\text{ann}-\text{nc}}{(p,q,q)}$</tex> and the set NC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ann</inf>(p,q of annular noncrossing partitions of {1, …, p+q} and observe that (unlike in the disc case) the natural map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{S}}_{\text{ann}-\text{nc}}{(p,q)}$</tex> onto NC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ann</inf>(p,q) has a pathology which prevents it from being injective. We point out that annular noncrossing permutations appear in the description of the second-order asymptotics for the joint moments of certain families (Wishart and GUE) of random matrices. Some of the formulas extend to a multiannular framework; as an application of that, we observe a phenomenon of asymptotic Gaussianity for traces of words made with independent Wishart matrices.

articleTitle: Stability for inverse resonance problem
abstract: For the Schrödinger operator on the half line, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varkappa^0={\{\varkappa^0\}}_1^\infty$</tex> is a sequence of zeroes (eigenvalues and resonances) of the Jost function for some real compactly supported potential q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varkappa-\varkappa^0\in\ell_\varepsilon^2$</tex> for some ε > 1, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varkappa$</tex> is the sequence of zeroes of the Jost function for some unique real compactly supported potential. Moreover, we show that the measure associated with the zeroes of the Jost function is a Carleson measure, and the sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum{(1+{\vert\varkappa_n^0\vert})}^{-p}$</tex> , p > 1, is estimated in terms of the Jost function.

articleTitle: Random matrices with external source and multiple orthogonal polynomials
abstract: We show that the average characteristic polynomial P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(z) = E [det(zI−M)] of the random Hermitian matrix ensemble <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_n^{-1}\operatorname{exp}{(-\text{Tr}{(\text{V}{(\text{M})}-AM)})}dM$</tex> is characterized by multiple orthogonality conditions that depend on the eigenvalues of the external source A. For each eigenvalue a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> of A, there is a weight, and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> has n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> orthogonality conditions with respect to this weight, if n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> is the multiplicity of a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>. The eigenvalue correlation functions have determinantal form, as shown by Zinn-Justin (1997). Here, we give a different expression for the kernel. We derive a Christoffel-Darboux formula in case A has two distinct eigenvalues, which leads to a compact formula in terms of a Riemann-Hilbert problem that is satisfied by multiple orthogonal polynomials.

articleTitle: Gap probability in the spectrum of random matrices and asymptotics of polynomials orthogonal on an arc of the unit circle
abstract: We obtain uniform asymptotics for polynomials orthogonal on a fixed and varying arc of the unit circle with a positive analytic weight function. We also complete the proof of the large s asymptotic expansion for the Fredholm determinant with the kernel sinz/(π z) on the interval [0,s], verifying a conjecture of Dyson for the constant term in the expansion. In the Gaussian unitary ensemble of random matrices, this determinant describes the probability for an interval of length s in the bulk scaling limit to be free from the eigenvalues.

articleTitle: Orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle: new results
abstract: We announce numerous new results in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle, most of which involve the connection between a measure on the unit circle in the complex plane and the coefficients in the recursion relations for the polynomials known as Verblunsky coefficients. Included are several applications of the recently discovered matrix realization of Cantero, Moral, and Velázquez. In analogy with the spectral theory of Jacobi matrices, several classes of exotic Verblunsky coefficients are studied. A version of Rahkmanov's theorem is proven with a single gap with eigenvalues allowed in the gap. Analogs of Borg's theorem and the Birman-Schwinger principle are found.

articleTitle: Weight-monodromy conjecture for certain threefolds in mixed characteristic
abstract: The weight-monodromy conjecture claims the coincidence of the weight filtration and the monodromy filtration, up to shift, on the l-adic étale cohomology of a proper smooth variety over a complete discrete valuation field. Although it has been proved in some cases, the case of dimension greater than or equal to 3 in mixed characteristic is still open so far. The aim of this paper is to give a proof of the weight-monodromy conjecture for a threefold which has a projective strictly semistable model such that, for each irreducible component of the special fiber, the Picard number is equal to the second l-adic Betti number. Our proof is based on a careful analysis of the weight spectral sequence of Rapoport and Zink by the Hodge index theorem for surfaces. We also prove a p-adic analogue by using the weight spectral sequence of Mokrane.

articleTitle: Potential theory of signed Riesz kernels: capacity and Hausdorff measure
abstract: In this paper, we study the natural capacity γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> related to the Riesz kernels x/∣x∣<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1 + α</sup> in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, where 0 < α < n. For noninteger α, an unexpected behaviour arises: for 0 < α < 1, compact sets in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> with finite α-Hausdorff measure have zero γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> capacity. In the Ahlfors-David regular case, for any noninteger index α, 0 < α < n, we prove that compact sets of finite α-Hausdorff measure have zero γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> capacity.

articleTitle: Hypergeometric theta functions and elliptic Macdonald polynomials
abstract: We introduce elliptic Macdonald polynomials associated with the 3-dimensional irreducible representation of sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Suitable limits of elliptic Macdonald polynomials are the standard Macdonald polynomials and conformal blocks. Identities for elliptic Macdonald polynomials, in particular, their modular properties, are studied.

articleTitle: Absolute tensor products
abstract: We calculate the absolute tensor product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta{(s,{\text{F}}_{p1})}\otimes\cdots\otimes\zeta{(s,{\text{F}}_{pr})}$</tex> by observing a relation between the multiple sine function of Shintani's type and Appell's O-function, or equivalently, the multiple elliptic gamma function. This allows us to give an Euler product expression for an absolute tensor product.

articleTitle: Compatible metrics on a manifold and nonlocal bi-Hamiltonian structures
abstract: Given a flat metric, one may generate a local Hamiltonian structure via the fundamental result of Dubrovin and Novikov. More generally, a flat pencil of metrics will generate a local bi-Hamiltonian structure, and with additional quasihomogeneity conditions, one obtains the structure of a Frobenius manifold. With appropriate curvature conditions, one may define a curved pencil of compatible metrics and these give rise to an associated nonlocal bi-Hamiltonian structure. Specific examples include the F-manifolds of Hertling and Manin equipped with an invariant metric. In this paper, the geometry supporting such compatible metrics is studied and interpreted in terms of a multiplication on the cotangent bundle. With additional quasihomogeneity assumptions, one arrives at a so-called weak <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> -manifold, a curved version of a Frobenius manifold (which is not, in general, an F-manifold). A submanifold theory is also developed.

articleTitle: On the symmetry of commuting differential operators with singularities along hyperplanes
abstract: We study the commutants of a Schrödinger operator whose potential function possesses inverse square singularities along some hyperplanes passing through the origin. It is shown that the Weyl group symmetry of the potential function and the commutants naturally results from such singularities and the generic nature of the coupling constants.

articleTitle: Hypergeometric solutions to the q-Painlevé equations
abstract: Hypergeometric solutions to seven q-Painlevé equations in Sakai's classification are constructed. Geometry of plane curves is used to reduce the q-Painlevé equations to the three-term recurrence relations for q-hypergeometric functions.

articleTitle: Nonlinear covers of real groups
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}$</tex> be a semisimple, simply connected algebraic group defined over ℝ. The set of real points G of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}$</tex> is not necessarily topologically simply connected, in which case G admits a nontrivial covering group. We give simple uniform proofs of several basic properties of real nonlinear groups, in particular, a simple criterion for when such a cover exists. Some of these properties were previously known from a case-by-case check based on the classification of real groups and their covers.

articleTitle: Discrete Painlevé equations, orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle, and N-recurrences for averages over U(N) —PIII′ and PV τ-functions
abstract: We show that the N × N Toeplitz determinants with the symbols <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z^\mu\operatorname{exp}{(-{(1/2)}\sqrt t{(z+1/z)})}$</tex> and (1+z)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup>(1+1/z)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ν</sup> exp(tz)—known τ-functions for the P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">III</inf>′ and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</inf> systems—are characterised by nonlinear recurrences for the reflection coefficients of the corresponding orthogonal polynomial system on the unit circle. It is shown that these recurrences are entirely equivalent to the discrete Painlevé equations associated with the degenerations of the rational surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_6^{(1)}\rightarrow E_7^{(1)}$</tex> (discrete Painlevé II) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_5^{(1)}\rightarrow E_6^{(1)}$</tex> (discrete Painlevé IV), respectively, through the algebraic methodology based upon the affine Weyl group symmetry of the Painlevé system, originally due to Okamoto. In addition, it is shown that the difference equations derived by methods based upon the Toeplitz lattice and Virasoro constraints, when reduced in order by exact summation, are equivalent to our recurrences. Expressions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_0F_{1}^{(1)},|{}_1F_{1}^{(1)}$</tex> are given for the reflection coefficients, respectively.

articleTitle: On the geometric simple connectivity of open manifolds
abstract: A manifold is said to be geometrically simply connected if it has a proper handle decomposition without 1-handles. By the work of Smale, for compact manifolds of dimension at least 5, this is equivalent to simple connectivity. We prove that there exists an obstruction to an open simply connected n-manifold of dimension n ≥ 5 being geometrically simply connected. In particular, for each n ≥ 4, there exist uncountably many simply connected n-manifolds which are not geometrically simply connected. We also prove that for n ≠ 4, an n-manifold proper homotopy equivalent to a weakly geometrically simply connected polyhedron is geometrically simply connected (for n = 4, it is only end-compressible). We analyze further the case n = 4 and Poénaru's conjecture.

articleTitle: De Rham model for string topology
abstract: Using the theory of iterated integrals, we give new short proofs of some of the main theorems of string topology including the one which relates Chas-Sullivan algebra structure on the homology of the free loop space of a simply connected closed oriented manifold to the Hochschild cohomology of the de Rham algebra.

articleTitle: A remark on Bohr's inequality
abstract: This paper studies the classical problem of determining the maximum growth of the Taylor series majorant of holomorphic functions with bound 1 in the unit disk, as a function of the radius of the Taylor series. We determine for the first time the asymptotic behavior of this maximum as the radius tends to 1, with a very small error term. The proof uses full asymptotic expansions of certain oscillatory integrals and the discrete Hilbert transform.

articleTitle: Bunches of cones in the divisor class group—a new combinatorial language for toric varieties
abstract: As an alternative to the description of a toric variety by a fan in the lattice of one-parameter subgroups, we present a new language in terms of what we call bunches—these are certain collections of cones in the vector space of rational divisor classes. The correspondence between these bunches and fans is based on the classical Gale duality. The new combinatorial language allows a much more natural description of geometric phenomena around divisors of toric varieties than the usual method by fans does. For example, the numerically effective cone and the ample cone of a toric variety can be read off immediately from its bunch. Moreover, the language of bunches appears to be useful for classification problems.

articleTitle: Abelian subalgebras in ℤ2-graded Lie algebras and affine Weyl groups
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{G}={\text{G}}_0\oplus{\text{G}}_1$</tex> be a simple ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-graded Lie algebra and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{b}}_0$</tex> be a fixed Borel subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{G}}_0$</tex> . We describe and enumerate the abelian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{b}}_0$</tex> -stable subalgebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{G}}_1$</tex> .

articleTitle: Relative framing of transverse knots
abstract: It is well known that a knot in a contact manifold (M,C) transverse to a trivialized contact structure possesses the natural framing given by the first of the trivialization vectors along the knot. If the Euler class e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> ∈ H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(M) of C is nonzero, then C is nontrivializable and the natural framing of transverse knots does not exist. We construct a new framing-type invariant of transverse knots called relative framing. It is defined for all tight C, all closed irreducible atoroidal M, and many other cases when the contact structure is not trivializable and the classical framing of transverse knots is not defined. We show that the relative framing distinguishes many transverse knots that are isotopic as unframed knots. Our recent result is that the groups of Vassiliev-Goussarov invariants of transverse and of framed knots are canonically isomorphic when C is trivialized and transverse knots have the natural framing. We show that the same result is true whenever the relative framing is well defined. As a useful tool, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert{\mathrm e}_\mathrm C{({\mathrm\alpha}_\ast{({\lbrack\mathrm F^2\rbrack})})}\vert}\leq\operatorname{max}{\{0,-\mathrm X{(\mathrm F^2)}\}}$</tex> for a tight (M,C) and a continuous mapping α : F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> → M of a closed oriented F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This generalizes Eliashberg's Bennequin-type inequality for embeddings α.

articleTitle: Necessary and sufficient conditions in the spectral theory of Jacobi matrices and Schrödinger operators
abstract: We announce three results in the theory of Jacobi matrices and Schrödinger operators. First, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for a measure to be the spectral measure of a Schrödinger operator −d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/dx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+V(x) on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0,∞) with V ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0,∞) and the boundary condition u(0) = 0. Second, we give necessary and sufficient conditions on the Jacobi parameters for the associated orthogonal polynomials to have Szegő asymptotics. Finally, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions on a measure to be the spectral measure of a Jacobi matrix with exponential decay at a given rate.

articleTitle: Greenberg's $\mathcal{L}$ -invariants of adjoint square Galois representations
abstract: For a two-dimensional p-adic Galois representation V associated to a p-ordinary Hecke eigen cusp form f of weight k ≥ 2, we identify the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}$</tex> -invariant (of Greenberg) of the (three-dimensional) adjoint square Ad(V) of V with the derivative of the p-coefficient of the Λ-adic lift of f. By this result, for a given p-adic analytic family of ordinary Hecke eigenforms, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}$</tex> -invariant does not vanish for almost all members in the p-adic family (as expected).

articleTitle: Sklyanin invariant integration
abstract: The Sklyanin algebra admits realizations by difference operators acting on theta functions. Sklyanin found an invariant metric for the action and conjectured an explicit formula for the corresponding reproducing kernel. We prove this conjecture and also give natural biorthogonal and orthogonal bases for the representation space. Moreover, we discuss connections with elliptic hypergeometric series and integrals and with elliptic 6j-symbols.

articleTitle: On the boundary of the Milnor fibre of nonisolated singularities (Erratum)
Defining equations of subspace arrangements embedded in reflection arrangements
abstract: We give explicit generators for ideals of two classes of subspace arrangements embedded in certain reflection arrangements, generalizing results of S.-Y. R. Li and W. C. W. Li, and Kleitman and Lovász. We also give minimal generators for the ideals of arrangements that arise in a natural way from the p-skeleton of an n-dimensional cube and discuss conditions under which the generators that we give form Gröbner bases.

articleTitle: Families index for pseudodifferential operators on manifolds with boundary
abstract: An analytic index is defined for a family of cusp pseudodifferential operators P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> on a fibration with fibres which are compact manifolds with boundaries, provided that the family is elliptic and has invertible indicial family at the boundary. In fact, there is always a perturbation Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> by a family of cusp operators of order −∞ such that each P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> + Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> is invertible. Thus, any elliptic family of symbols has a realization as an invertible family of cusp pseudodifferential operators, which is a form of the cobordism invariance of the index. A crucial role is played by the weak contractibility of the group of cusp smoothing operators on a compact manifold with nontrivial boundary and the associated exact sequence of classifying spaces of odd and even K-theory.

articleTitle: GKM theory for torus actions with nonisolated fixed Points
abstract: Let M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2d</sup> be a compact symplectic manifold and T a compact n-dimensional torus. A Hamiltonian action, τ, of T on M is a GKM action if, for every p ∈ M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup>, the isotropy representation of T on T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>M has pairwise linearly independent weights. For such an action, the image of the set of zero- and one-dimensional orbits under the projection onto M/T is aregular d-valent graph; Goresky, Kottwitz, and MacPherson have proved that the equivariant cohomology of M can be computed from the combinatorics of this graph. In this paper we define a “GKM action with nonisolated fixed points” to be an action, τ, of T on M with the property that for every connected component, F of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup> and p ∈ F, the isotropy representation of T on the normal space to F at p has pairwise linearly independent weights. For such an action, we show that all components of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup> are diffeomorphic and prove an analogue of the theorem above.

articleTitle: A new proof of Steinberg's fixed-point theorem
abstract: We give a short proof, using only elementary invariant theory, of Steinberg's theorem that if a group acting on a complex space is generated by unitary reflections, then the isotropy subgroup of any point in the space is again a reflection group.

articleTitle: A stacky semistable reduction theorem
abstract: Let X be a proper regular scheme over a complete discrete valuation ring R of equicharacteristic 0 such that the generic fiber of X is smooth and the reduced closed fiber is a divisor with normal crossings. We show that after making a finite extension R′ of R, there exists a proper semistable Delign-Mumford stack X over R′ whose generic fiber agrees with the base change of X. Furthermore, the stack X admits a natural action of the Galois group of R′ over R extending the action on the generic fiber. This result can be viewed as a stack-theoretic version of the semistable reduction theorem of Kempf, Knudsen, Mumford, and Saint-Donat.

articleTitle: L-functions of exponential sums over one-dimensional affinoids: Newton over Hodge
abstract: This paper proves a sharp lower bound for Newton polygons of L-functions of exponential sums of one-variable rational functions. Let p be a prime and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{\text{F}}}_p$</tex> be the algebraic closure of the finite field of p elements. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline f{(x)}$</tex> be any one-variable rational function over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{\text{F}}}_p$</tex> with ℓ poles of orders d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>. Suppose p is coprime to d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>. We prove that there exists a tight lower bound which we call Hodge polygon, depending only on the d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>'s, to the Newton polygon of L-function of exponential sums of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline f{(x)}$</tex> . Moreover, we show that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline f{(x)}$</tex> these two polygons coincide if and only if p ≡ 1 mod d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> for every 1 ≤ j ≤ ℓ. As a corollary, we obtain a tight lower bound for the p-adic Newton polygon of zeta-function of an Artin-Schreier curve given by affine equations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y^p-y=\overline f{(x)}$</tex> .

articleTitle: Long-time existence for small data nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations on tori and spheres
abstract: Consider a nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation on a compact manifold M with smooth Cauchy data of size ε → 0. Denote by T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf> the maximal time of existence of a smooth solution. One always has T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf> ≥ c ε<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−k+1</sup> if the nonlinearity vanishes at order k at 0. We prove that when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M=\text{T}^d$</tex> , k=2, and the equation is quasilinear, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf> ≥ cε<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M=\text{S}^{d-1}$</tex> , the equation is semilinear, and k = 2p, we show that T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf> ≥ cε<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2p</sup> for almost every mass. The proof of these results relies on a systematic use of normal forms methods.

articleTitle: Automatic uniformity
abstract: Let X be an algebraic variety over the algebraically closed field K and Ξ ⊆ X(K) a set of K-rational points on X. We say that a subvariety Y ⊆ X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> of some Cartesian power of X is Ξ-special if Ξ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> ∩ Y(K) is Zariski dense in Y. We show under certain hypotheses on Ξ, for instance, that the class of Ξ-special varieties is closed under intersections, that when subvarieties of X vary in an algebraic family, the Zariski closures of their intersections with Ξ also vary uniformly. As a special case, we see that if the André-Oort conjecture holds, then for each g, n, and d, there is a constant B = B(g,n,d) such that if C is a curve of degree d in the moduli space of g-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties with full-level n structure, either C is a modular curve or C contains at most B CM-moduli points.

articleTitle: Semisimple quantum cohomology and blowups
abstract: Using results of Gathmann, we prove: if a smooth projective variety X has generically semisimple (p,p)-quantum cohomology, then the same is true for the blowup of X at any number of points. This is a successful test for a modified version of Dubrovin's conjecture from the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) 1998.

articleTitle: Trace forms of Galois extensions in the presence of a fourth root of unity
abstract: We study quadratic forms that can occur as trace forms q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L/K</inf> of Galois field extensions L/K, under the assumption that K contains a primitive fourth root of unity. M. Epkenhans conjectured that q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L/K</inf> is always a scaled Pfister form. We prove this conjecture and classify the finite groups G which admit a G-Galois extension L/K with a nonhyperbolic trace form. We also give several applications of these results.

articleTitle: Double affine Hecke algebras of rank 1 and affine cubic surfaces
abstract: We study the algebraic properties of the five-parameter family H(t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>;q) of double affine Hecke algebras of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^\vee C_1$</tex> . This family generalizes Cherednik's double affine Hecke algebras of rank 1. It was introduced by Sahi and studied by Noumi and Stokman as an algebraic structure which controls Askey-Wilson polynomials. We show that if q=1, then the spectrum of the center of H is an affine cubic surface C, obtained from a projective one by removing a triangle consisting of smooth points. Moreover, any such surface is obtained as the spectrum of the center of H for some values of parameters. This result allows one to give a simple geometric description of the action of an extension of PGL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ) by ℤ on the center of H. When C is smooth, it admits a unique algebraic symplectic structure, and the spherical subalgebra eHe of the algebra H for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q=e^\hslash$</tex> provides its deformation quantization. Using that H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(C,ℂ)=ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>, we find that the Hochschild cohomology HH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(H) (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q=e^\hslash$</tex> ) is five-dimensional for generic parameter values. From this we deduce that the only deformations of H come from variations of parameters. This explains from the point of view of noncommutative geometry why one cannot add more parameters into the theory of Askey-Wilson polynomials. We also prove that the five-parameter family H(t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>;q) of algebras yields the universal deformation of the semidirect product q-Weyl algebra with Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and that the family of cubic surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C=C_{\underline t}$</tex> , <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\underline t\in\text{3/8}_{\underline t}^4$</tex> , gives the universal deformation of the Poisson algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{3/8}\lbrack X^{\pm1},P^{\pm1}\rbrack^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$</tex> .

articleTitle: Rational vertex operator algebras and the effective central charge
abstract: We establish that the Lie algebra of weight 1 states in a (strongly) rational vertex operator algebra is reductive, and that its Lie rank 1 is bounded above by the effective central charge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde c$</tex> . We show that lattice vertex operator algebras may be characterized by the equalities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde c=l=c$</tex> , and in particular holomorphic lattice theories may be characterized among all holomorphic vertex operator algebras by the equality l = c.

articleTitle: Semiclassical analysis of generic codimension 3 crossings
abstract: We study a family of solutions to a system of two equations which display a codimension 3 generic crossing: the crossing set is a symplectic submanifold of the phase space. We consider initial data which are bounded families in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. We obtain a quantitative description of the energy transfer above the crossing in terms of two-scale Wigner measures. We prove first that this transfer concerns the part of the energy localized at finite distance, with respect to the scale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt h$</tex> , of the sets of all the ingoing classical trajectories. Provided a generalization of two-scale Wigner measures to the case of symplectic submanifolds, we split the Wigner measure of families of solutions into a countable sum of positive Radon measures. The energy transfer at the crossing is described by Landau-Zener formula for the terms of this decomposition.

articleTitle: Virtual first Betti number and integrality of compact complex two-ball quotients
abstract: We prove that for a compact complex hyperbolic space form of complex dimension two whose associated lattice is nonintegral, the first Betti number is virtually positive. This provides support to a question of Borel in favor of a conjecture of Thurston on virtual positivity of the first Betti number on complex hyperbolic space forms. The result can also be considered as a topological sufficient condition for the integrality of a lattice in PU(2,1).

articleTitle: On G-function of Frobenius manifolds related to Hurwitz spaces
abstract: The semisimple Frobenius manifolds related to the Hurwitz spaces H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g, N</inf>(k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>) are considered. We show that the corresponding isomonodromic tau-function τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</inf> coincides with (−1/2)-power of the Bergmann tau-function which was introduced in a recent work by the authors. This enables us to calculate explicitly the G-function of Frobenius manifolds related to the Hurwitz spaces H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, N</inf>(k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1, N</inf>(k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>. As simple consequences we get formulas for the G-functions of the Frobenius manifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{3/8}^N/\widetilde W^k{(A_{N-1})}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{3/8}\times\text{3/8}^{N-1}\times{\{\Im z>0\}}/J{(A_{N-1})}$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde W^k{(A_{N-1})}$</tex> is an extended affine Weyl group and J(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N−1</inf>) is a Jacobi group, in particular, proving the conjecture of Strachan (2003). In case of Frobenius manifolds related to Hurwitz spaces H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g, N</inf>(k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>) with g ≥ 2, we obtain formulas for ∣τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</inf>∣<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> which allow to compute the real part of the G-function.

articleTitle: Matrix models for circular ensembles
abstract: The Gibbs distribution for n particles of the Coulomb gas on the unit circle at inverse temperature β is given by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{E}_n^\beta(f)=(1/Z_{n,\beta})\int\cdots\int f(e^{i\theta_1},\dots,e^{i\theta_n}){\vert\Delta(e^{i\theta_1},\dots,e^{i\theta_n})\:\vert}^\beta(d\theta_1/2\pi)\dots d\theta_n/2\pi$</tex> for any symmetric function f, where Δ denotes the Vandermonde determinant and Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n,β</inf> the normalization constant. We will describe an ensemble of (sparse) random matrices whose eigenvalues follow this distribution. Our approach combines elements from the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle with ideas from a recent work of Dumitriu and Edelman. In particular, we resolve a question left open by them: finding a tridiagonal model for the Jacobi ensemble.

articleTitle: Hankel operators on Bergman spaces and similarity to contractions
abstract: We consider Foguel-Hankel operators on vector-valued Bergman spaces. Such operators defined on Hardy spaces play a central role in the famous example by Pisier of a polynomially bounded operator which is not similar to a contraction. On Bergman spaces we encounter a completely different behaviour; power boundedness, polynomial boundedness, and similarity to a contraction are all equivalent for this class of operators.

articleTitle: The Alexander module of links at infinity
abstract: Neumann (1989) showed that the topology of a “regular” algebraic curve V ⊂ ℂ <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is determined up to proper isotopy by some link in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> called the link at infinity of V. In this paper, we compute the Alexander module over ℂ[t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">± 1</sup>] of any such link at infinity.

articleTitle: Nonlinear instability of ideal plane flows
abstract: We study nonlinear instability of stationary ideal plane flows. For any bounded domain and very general steady flows, we show that if the linearized equation has an exponentially growing solution, then the steady flow is nonlinearly unstable. The nonlinear instability is in the sense that we can find an initial perturbation arbitrarily close to the steady flow such that the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> norm of the velocity perturbation grows exponentially beyond a fixed value. The same result is also proved for the Charney-Hasegawa-Mima equation.

articleTitle: Remarks on zeta regularized products
abstract: The zeta regularized products play important roles in constructing functions having a certain invariance and a given set of zeros. To deal with wider class of sequences, we introduce an extended version of regularized products. It allows us to treat the case where the attached zeta function has even a log singularity at the origin. In fact, we need the meromorphy of the zeta function for zeta regularizations so far. We discuss examples of the regularized products of sinh(ρ−x)′s especially when ρ runs over the essential zeros of zeta functions.

articleTitle: Motivic nature of character values of depth-zero representations
abstract: It is shown that the values of Harish-Chandra distribution characters on definable compact subsets of the set of topologically unipotent elements of some reductive p-adic groups can be expressed as the trace of Frobenius action on certain geometric objects, namely, Chow motives. The result is restricted to a class of depth-zero representations of symplectic or special orthogonal groups that can be obtained by inflation from Deligne-Lusztig representations. The proof works both in positive and zero characteristic, and relies on arithmetic motivic integration.

articleTitle: Positivity of Dunkl's intertwining operator via the trigonometric setting
abstract: A new proof for the positivity of Dunkl's intertwining operator in the crystallographic case is given. It is based on an asymptotic relationship between the Opdam-Cherednik kernel and the Dunkl kernel as recently observed by M. de Jeu, and on positivity results of S. Sahi for the Heckman-Opdam polynomials and their nonsymmetric counterparts.

articleTitle: Classifying real polynomial pencils
abstract: We identify ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> with the space of real homogeneous polynomials of degree n in two variables considered up to a scalar factor. The standard discriminant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{D}}_{n+1}\subset \mathbb{RP}^n$</tex> is Whitney-stratified according to the number and the multiplicities of multiple real zeros. A real polynomial pencil, that is, a line L ⊂ ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, is called generic if it intersects <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{D}}_{n+1}$</tex> transversally. Nongeneric pencils form theGrassmann discriminant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{D}}_{2,n+1}\subset G_{2,n+1}$</tex> , where G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,n+1</inf> is the Grassmannian of lines in ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. We enumerate the connectedcomponents of the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde G_{2,n+1}=G_{2,n+1}\setminus \mathcal{D}_{2,n+1}$</tex> of all generic lines in ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and relate this topic to the Hawaii conjecture and the classical theorems of Obreschkoff and Hermite-Biehler.

articleTitle: Some estimates for non-microstates free entropy dimension with applications to q-semicircular families
abstract: We give a general estimate for the nonmicrostates free entropy dimension δ*(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>). If X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> generate a diffuse von Neumann algebra, we prove that δ*X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> ≥ 1. In the case that X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> are q-semicircular variables as introduced by Bozejko and Speicher and q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>n < 1, we show that δ*X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> > 1. We also show that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert\mathrm q\vert}<\sqrt2-1$</tex> , the von Neumann algebras generated by a finite family of q-Gaussian random variables satisfy a condition of Ozawa and are therefore solid: the relative commutant of any diffuse subalgebra must be hyperfinite. In particular, when these algebras are factors, they are prime and do not have property Γ.

articleTitle: Appell polynomials and their relatives
abstract: This paper summarizes some known results about Appell polynomials and investigates their various analogs. The primary of these are the free Appell polynomials. In the multivariate case, they can be considered as natural analogs of the Appell polynomials among polynomials in noncommuting variables. They also fit well into the framework of free probability. For the free Appell polynomials, a number of combinatorial and “diagram” formulas are proven, such as the formulas for their linearization coefficients. An explicit formula for their generating function is obtained. These polynomials are also martingales for free Lévy processes. For more general free Sheffer families, a necessary condition for pseudo-orthogonality is given. Another family investigated is that of the Kailath-Segall polynomials. These are multivariate polynomials, which share with the Appell polynomials nice combinatorial properties, but are always orthogonal. Their origins lie in the Fock space representations, or in the theory of multiple stochastic integrals. Diagram formulas are proven for these polynomials as well, even in the q-deformed case.

articleTitle: A formula for K-theory truncation Schubert calculus
abstract: Define a truncation r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>(p of a polynomial p in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{x_1,x_2,x_3,\dots\}$</tex> as the polynomial with all but the first t variables set to zero. In certain good cases, the truncation of a Schubert or Grothendieck polynomial may again be a Schubert or Grothendieck polynomial. We use this phenomenon to give subtraction-free formulas for certain Schubert structure constants in K(Flags(ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>), in particular generalizing those studied by Kogan (2001) in which only cohomology was treated, and those studied by Buch (2002) on the Grassmannian case. The terms in the answer are computed using “marching” operations on permutation diagrams.

articleTitle: Planar open book decompositions and contact structures
abstract: We observe that while all overtwisted contact structures on compact 3-manifolds are supported by planar open book decompositions, not all contact structures are. This has relevance to the Weinstein conjecture and invariants of contact structures.

articleTitle: A cuspidality criterion for the functorial product on GL(2) × GL(3) with a cohomological application
abstract: For all cusp forms π on GL(3) and π′ on GL(2) over a number field F, H. Kim and F. Shahidi have functorially associated an automorphic form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi=\pi\boxtimes\pi^{'}$</tex> on GL(6) such that L(s, Π) agrees with the Rankin-Selberg L-function of the pair (π, π′). First we establish a criterion as to when Π is cuspidal. Then we apply it to construct non-self-dual, nonmonomial cuspidal cohomology classes for suitable congruence subgroups of SL(3, ℤ). We also analyze the Galois image of certain related ℓ-adic representations.

articleTitle: Green-Lazarsfeld gonality conjecture for a generic curve of odd genus
abstract: We prove the gonality conjecture of Green and Lazarsfeld for generic curves of odd genus. The even-genus case was previously solved in a joint work with Claire Voisin. The proof uses, among other things, Green's syzygy canonical conjecture for generic curves of odd genus.

articleTitle: Dynamique des correspondances algébriques et hauteurs
abstract: The Néron-Tate height on an abelian variety is known to be constructed from any Weil height by a dynamical process. Similarly, we wish to obtain (dynamically) the Faltings height on a moduli space of abelian varieties by iterating a Hecke correspondence. In this direction, we study the convergence of metrics under this iteration. As an application, we give formulas on the average height of isogenous QM abelian surfaces.

articleTitle: The correspondence between KdV and Camassa-Holm
abstract: We show that the Liouville transformation relating the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) and Camassa-Holm isospectral problems gives a direct correspondence between the KdV and Camassa-Holm hierarchies.

articleTitle: Deformation of Weyl modules and generalized parking functions
abstract: Local Weyl modules over two-dimensional currents with values in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{G}l_r$</tex> are deformed into spaces with bases related to parking functions. Using this construction, we (1) propose a simple proof that dimension of the space of diagonal coinvariants is not less than the number of parking functions; (2) describe the limits of Weyl modules in terms of semi-infinite forms and find the limits of characters; and (3) propose a lower bound and state a conjecture for dimensions of Weyl modules with arbitrary highest weights. Also we express characters of deformed Weyl modules in terms of ρ-parking functions and the Frobenius characteristic map.

articleTitle: Absolutely continuous spectrum of multidimensional Schrödinger operator
abstract: We prove that a three-dimensional Schrödinger operator with slowly decaying potential has an absolutely continuous (a.c.) spectrum that fills ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. Asymptotics of Green's functions is obtained as well.

articleTitle: Classification of fusion categories of dimension pq
abstract: We provide a complete classification of fusion categories of Frobenius-Perron (FP) dimension pq over complex numbers, where p < q are distinct primes, thus giving a categorical generalization of the classification of semisimple Hopf algebras of dimension pq given by the first two authors in 1998. As a corollary, we also obtain a classification of semisimple quasi-Hopf algebras of dimension pq. We also obtain a classification of finite-dimensional semisimple quasi-Hopf (in particular, Hopf) algebras whose irreducible representations have dimensions 1 and n such that the 1-dimensional representations form a cyclic group of order n. All such quasi-Hopf algebras turn out to be group theoretical. Finally, we classify fusion categories whose invertible objects form a cyclic group of order n > 1 and which have only one noninvertible object of dimension n.

articleTitle: Irreducibility of the Siegel moduli spaces with parahoric level structure
abstract: We prove that the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{A}}_{g,\Gamma_0{(p)}}\otimes{\overline{\text{F}}}_p$</tex> of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g with a Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(p)-level structure in characteristic p has 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup> irreducible components. The cases of other parahoric level structures are also considered.

articleTitle: Singular polynomials for the symmetric groups
abstract: For certain negative rational numbers κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, called singular values and associated with the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> on N objects, there exist homogeneous polynomials annihilated by each Dunkl operator when the parameter κ=κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. It was shown by the author, de Jeu, and Opdam (1994) that the singular values are exactly the values −m/n with 2 ≤ n ≤ N, m=1,2,…, and m/n is not an integer. This paper constructs for each pair (m,n) satisfying these conditions an irreducible S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>-module of singular polynomials for the singular value −m/n. These singular polynomials are special cases of nonsymmetric Jack polynomials. The paper presents some formulae for the action of Dunkl operators on these polynomials valid in general, and a method for showing the dependence of poles (in the parameter κ) on the number of variables. Murphy elements are used to analyze the representation of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> on irreducible spaces of singular polynomials.

articleTitle: Boundary spectral behavior for semiclassical operators in dimension one
abstract: For a class of nonselfadjoint semiclassical operators in dimension one, we get a complete asymptotic description of all eigenvalues near a critical value of the leading symbol of the operator on the boundary of the pseudospectrum.

articleTitle: E8-plumbings and exotic contact structures on spheres
abstract: We prove the existence of exotic but homotopically trivial contact structures on spheres of dimension 8k−1. Together with previous results of Eliashberg and the second author, this proves the existence of such structures on all odd-dimensional spheres. Here, a contact structure is called “exotic” if it is not diffeomorphic to the standard contact structure; “homotopically trivial” means that it induces, like the standard structure, an almost complex structure along the sphere that extends over a cobounding disc. The construction is based on finding certain highly connected symplectic manifolds, with boundary a sphere, via plumbings of disc bundles. Exoticity of the induced contact structure on the boundary follows from a result of Eliashberg, Floer, Gromov, and McDuff about symplectic fillings of the standard contact structure.

articleTitle: On the generic unitary dual of quasisplit classical groups
abstract: We classify the irreducible unitarizable representations ofclassical groups over a local field of characteristic 0 which admit a Whittaker model with respect to a nondegenerate character. The classification is in terms of the Langlands data of the representation. It is analogous to the classification of unramified representations of classical groups obtained by Barbasch and Moy.

articleTitle: Metrics of positive Ricci curvature on bundles
abstract: We construct new examples of manifolds of positive Ricci curvature which, topologically, are vector bundles over compact manifolds of almost nonnegative Ricci curvature. In particular, we prove that if E is the total space of a vector bundle over a compact manifold of nonnegative Ricci curvature, then E × ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> admits a complete metric of positive Ricci curvature for all large p.

articleTitle: Resonances for magnetic Stark Hamiltonians in two-dimensional case
abstract: We study the resonances of the two-dimensional Schrödinger operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_1{(B;\beta)}={(D_x-By)}^2+D_y^2+\beta x+V{(x,y)}$</tex> , B > 0, β > 0, with constant magnetic and electric fields. We define the resonances of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(B; β) and the spectral shift function ξ(λ) related to P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(B; β) and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(B; β) = P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(B; β) − V(x, y) without any restriction on B and β. For strong magnetic fields (B → ∞) we obtain a representation of the derivative of ξ(λ), a trace formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tr}{(f{(P_1{(B;\beta)})}-f{(P_0{(B;\beta)})})}$</tex> and an upper bound for the number of the resonances lying in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{z\in{3/8}\text{:}{\vert\Re_z-{(2n-1)}B\vert}\leq\alpha B$</tex> , <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Im}z\geq\mu\operatorname{Im}\theta\}$</tex> , 0 < α < 1, 0 < μ < 1, Im θ < 0. Moreover, for B → ∞ we examine the resonance-free domains and show that the resonances are included in the neighborhoods <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{z\in 3/8\text{:}{\vert\Re_z-{(2n-1)}B\vert}\leq C_0\}$</tex> , where (2n − 1)B are the Landau levelsand C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> > 0 is a constant independent of B and n ∈ ℕ* = ℕ \ {0}.

articleTitle: Analogue of Kostant's u-cohomology formula for the general linear superalgebra
abstract: We determine in an explicit form the Lie superalgebra cohomology groups of the upper triangular odd subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\text{Gl}}_{\text{m}\vert\text{n}})_{+1}$</tex> of the general linear superalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{Gl}}_{\text{m}\vert\text{n}}$</tex> with coefficients in irreducible tensor modules over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{Gl}}_{\text{m}\vert\text{n}}$</tex> . Using this, we develop a Weyl-type character formula for the irreducible tensor representations. Both in the computation of the cohomology groups and in the construction of the character formula, the Weyl group of the infinite-rank affine Kac-Moody algebra of A-type plays an essential role.

articleTitle: An improved local well-posedness result for the modified KdV equation
abstract: The Cauchy problem for the modified KdV equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_t+u_{xxx}={(u^3)}_x$</tex> , u(0)=u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, is shown to be locally well posed for data u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{H_s^r}{(\mathbb{R})}$</tex> defined by the norm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Arrowvert u_{0}\Arrowvert_{\widehat{H_s^r}}:={\Arrowvert\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat{u_0}L_\xi^{r^{'}}\Arrowvert}$</tex> , provided 4/3 < r ≤ 2, s ≥ 1/2 − 1/2r. For r=2, this coincides with the best possible result on the H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>-scale due to Kenig, Ponce, and Vega. The proof uses an appropriate variant of the Fourier restriction norm method and linear as well as bilinear estimates for the solutions of the Airy equation.

articleTitle: The non-Abelian momentum map for Poisson-Lie symmetries on the chiral WZNW phase space
abstract: The gauge action of the Lie group G on the chiral Wess-Zumino-Novikov-Witten (WZNW) phase space ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ǧ</inf> of quasiperiodic fields with Ǧ-valued monodromy, where Ǧ ⊂ G is an open submanifold, is known to be a Poisson-Lie (PL) action with respect to any coboundary PL structure on G, if the Poisson bracket on ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ǧ</inf> is defined by a suitable monodromy-dependent exchange r-matrix. We describe the momentum map for these symmetries when G is either a factorizable PL group or a compact simple Lie group with its standard PL structure. The main result is an explicit one-to-one correspondence between the monodromy variable M ∈ Ǧ and a conventional variable Ω ∈ G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>. This permits us to convert the PL groupoid associated with a WZNW exchange r-matrix into a “canonical” PL groupoid constructed from the Heisenberg double of G, and consequently to obtain a natural PL generalization of the classical dynamical Yang-Baxter equation.

articleTitle: Diagonal coinvariants and double affine Hecke algebras
abstract: We establish a q-generalization of Gordon's theorem which states that the space of diagonal coinvariants has a quotient identified with a perfect representation of the rational double affine Hecke algebra. This generalization leads to a simple proof of his theorem and relates it to the Weyl algebras at roots of unity. We introduce the universal double affine Hecke algebra and the corresponding universal Dunkl operators acting in noncommutative polynomials in terms of two sets of variables.

articleTitle: Global fold structure of the Miura map on $L^2{(\text{T})}$
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to study the Miura transform r → r′ + r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-functions. More precisely, we prove that the Miura transform, viewed as map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2{(\text{T})}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{-1}{(\text{T})}$</tex> , has a global fold structure with a “Whitney type” singularity at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_0^2{(\text{T})}$</tex> , the space of periodic L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-functions with mean zero. Using the well-known fact that the Miura transform maps solutions of the modified Korteweg-de Vries equation (mKdV) to solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV), the above result can be used as a tool to obtain low-regularity well-posedness results for mKdV on the circle from corresponding low-regularity well-posedness results of KdV (and vice versa).

articleTitle: The amount of discrete spectrum of a perturbed periodic Schrödinger operator inside a fixed interval (λ1,λ2)
abstract: Let A be a periodic Schrödinger operator and let V ≥ 0 be a decaying potential. We study the number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde N{(\alpha)}$</tex> of the eigenvalues of the operator A(α)=A−α V inside a fixed interval (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). We obtain an asymptotic formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde N{(\alpha)}$</tex> as α → ∞. In this paper we extend the results of Safronov (2001) for a more general class of perturbations.

articleTitle: An analogue of Radford's S4 formula for finite tensor categories
abstract: We develop the theory of Hopf bimodules for a finite rigid tensor category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}$</tex> . Then we use this theory to define a distinguished invertible object D of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}$</tex> and an isomorphism of tensor functors <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm\delta:\mathrm V^{\ast\ast}\rightarrow\mathrm D\otimes^{\ast\ast}\mathrm V\otimes\mathrm D^{-1}$</tex> . This provides a categorical generalization of Radford's S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras (presented in 1976), which was proved by Nikshych (2002) for weak Hopf algebras and by Hausser and Nill (1999) for quasi-Hopf algebras, and was conjectured in general by Etingof and Ostrik (2003). When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}$</tex> is braided, we establish a connection between δ and the Drinfeld isomorphism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}$</tex> , extending the result of Radford (1992). We also show that a factorizable braided tensor category is unimodular (i.e., D=1). Finally, we apply our theory to prove that the pivotalization of a fusion category is spherical, and give a purely algebraic characterization of exact module categories defined by Etingof and Ostrik (2003).

articleTitle: On the complex moments of symmetric power L-functions at s = 1
abstract: The study of the distribution values of L-functions at the point s = 1 is a classical topic in analytic number theory which goes back to Chowla and Erdös. For some time, this question has been limited to the case of Euler products of degree 1, and it is only recently that the case of L-functions of higher degree was investigated, firstly by Luo and then by Royer et al., namely, for the standard and the symmetric square L-functions of modular forms. In this paper we propose a conceptual approach to analyzing the distribution of values at s = 1 of automorphic L-functions for appropriate families of automorphic forms. We illustrate this by computing arbitrary complex moments of arbitrary symmetric power L-functions of holomorphic forms of large (prime) level at s = 1 (assuming that the corresponding L-functions are automorphic, as is predicted by the Langlands functoriality conjectures and effectively proved for the symmetric powers up to 4). In addition, we provide a natural probabilistic interpretation of these computations. Our approach should generalize to quite arbitrary L-functions of appropriate families of automorphic forms.

articleTitle: Multivariate Igusa theory: decay rates of exponential sums
abstract: We obtain general estimates for exponential integrals of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_f{(y)}=\int_{\mathbb{Z}_p^n}\psi{(\sum\nolimits_{j=1}^ry_jf_j{(x)})}{\vert dx\vert}$</tex> , where the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> are restricted power series over ℚ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> ε ℚ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> and ψ is a nontrivial additive character on ℚ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>. We prove that if (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) is a dominant map, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert E_f{(y)}\vert}<c{\vert y\vert}^\alpha$</tex> for some c > 0 and α < 0, uniform in y, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert y\vert=\operatorname{max}(\vert y_i\vert)_i$</tex> . In fact, we obtain similar estimates for a much bigger class of exponential integrals. To prove these estimates we introduce a new method to study exponential sums, namely, we use the theory of p-adic subanalytic sets and p-adic integration techniques based on p-adic cell decomposition. We compare our results with some elementarily obtained explicit bounds for E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> with f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> polynomials.

articleTitle: Nonvanishing twists of $\text{GL}{(2)}$ automorphic L-functions
abstract: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GL}{(2,{\text{A}}_K)}$</tex> . Given any prime integer n, suppose there exists a single nonvanishing nth-order twist of the L-series associated to π at the center of the critical strip. We use the method of multiple Dirichlet series to establish that there exist infinitely many such nonvanishing nth-order twists of the L-series of the representation at the center.

articleTitle: Path model for quantum loop modules of fundamental type
abstract: We study z-crystal bases of simple integrable modules of level zero over a quantised affine algebra. We establish their existence for some class of such modules and show that they admit a combinatorial realisation in the framework of the path model of Littelmann.

articleTitle: Projective complete cohomological dimension of a group
abstract: Let G be an arbitrary group. The projective complete cohomological dimension of G, denoted by pccd G, is the least integer n for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^i{(G,-)}\approx\widehat H^i{(G,-)}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i > n$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{H}^i(G,-)$</tex> is the complete cohomology of G. We study the properties of projective complete cohomological dimension of a group and then, using these, we give partial answers to three conjectures formulated by Ikenaga, Kropholler, and Talelli.

articleTitle: On steady gravity waves with vorticity
abstract: Using bifurcation theory and methods from the Schauder theory of elliptic partial differential equations, we prove the existence of small-amplitude steady water waves with an arbitrary vorticity distribution.

articleTitle: Lattice points in cones and Dirichlet series
abstract: Hecke proved the meromorphic continuation of a Dirichlet series associated to the lattice points in a triangle with a real quadratic slope and found the possible poles in terms of the fundamental unit. An analogous result is proven for certain elliptical cones where now the poles are determined by the spectrum of the Laplacian on an arithmetic Riemann surface.

articleTitle: On the Fox-Milnor theorem for the Alexander polynomial of links
