abstract: We show that the Alexander polynomial Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>(t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</inf>) of a link L in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> bounding a smooth compact oriented surface in B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> with μ connected components and Euler characteristic 1 is of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p{(t_1,\dots,t_\mu)}p{(t_1^{-1},\dots,t_\mu^{-1})}$</tex> for p ∈ ℤ[t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</inf>], up to a unit and factors t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>−1.

articleTitle: Associated primes of local cohomology modules and of Frobenius powers
abstract: We construct normal hypersurfaces whose local cohomology modules have infinitely many associated primes. These include unique factorization domains of characteristic zero with rational singularities as well as F-regular unique factorization domains of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we answer a question on the associated primes of Frobenius powers of ideals, which arose from the localization problem in tight closure theory.

articleTitle: Some elementary theorems about divisibility of 0-cycles on abelian varieties defined over finite fields
abstract: If X is an abelian variety over a field, and L ∈ Pic(X), we know that the degree of the 0-cycle L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup> is divisible by g!. As a 0-cycle, it is not, even over a field of cohomological dimension 1, but we show that over a finite field, there is some hope.

articleTitle: Flows with Lyapunov one-forms and a generalization of Farber's theorem on homoclinic cycles
abstract: We prove that if a flow on a compact manifold admits a Lyapunov one-form with small zero set Y, then there must exist a generalized homoclinic cycle, that is, a cyclically ordered chain of orbits outside Y such that for every consecutive pair the forward limit set of one and the backward limit set of the next are both contained in the same connected component of Y. The smallness of the zero set is measured in terms of a category-type invariant associated to the cohomology class of the form that was recently introduced by Farber (2002).

articleTitle: Théorème de Dobrowolski-Laurent pour les extensions abéliennes sur une courbe elliptique à multiplication complexe
abstract: Let E/K be an elliptic curve with complex multiplication and let K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ab</sup> be the Abelian closure of K. We prove that there exists a constant c(E/K) such that for all point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P\in E{(\overline K)}\backslash E_\text tors$</tex> , we have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat h{(P)}\geq{(c{(E/K)}/D)}{(\operatorname{log}\operatorname{log}5D/\operatorname{log}2D)}^{13}$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D={\lbrack K^\text ab{(P)}:K^\text ab\rbrack}$</tex> . This result extends to the case of elliptic curves with complex multiplication the previous result of Amoroso-Zannier (2000) on the analogous problem on the multiplicative group G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, and generalizes to the case of extensions of degree D the result of Baker (2003) on the lower bound of the Néron-Tate height of the points defined over an Abelian extension of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication. This result also enables us to simplify the proof of a theorem of Viada (2003).

articleTitle: Stability theorems for symplectic and contact pairs
abstract: We prove Gray-Moser stability theorems for complementary pairs of forms of constant class defining symplectic pairs, contact-symplectic pairs, and contact pairs. We also consider the case of contact-symplectic and contact-contact structures in which the constant class condition on a one-form is replaced by the condition that its kernel hyperplane distribution have constant class in the sense of É. Cartan.

articleTitle: Monopole classes and Einstein metrics
abstract: We introduce the notion of a special monopole class on a four-manifold. This is used to prove restrictions on the smooth structures of Einstein manifolds. As an application, we prove that there are Einstein four-manifolds which are simply connected, spin, and satisfy the strict Hitchin-Thorpe inequality, and which are homeomorphic to manifolds without Einstein metrics.

articleTitle: A proof of the q,t-Schröder conjecture
abstract: We prove a recent conjecture of Egge, Haglund, Killpatrick, and Kremer (2003), which gives a combinatorial formula for the coefficients of a hook shape in the Schur function expansion of the symmetric function ∇ e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, which Haiman (2002) has shown to have a representation-theoretic interpretation. More precisely, we show that 〈∇e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−d</inf>h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>〉 can be expressed as ∑ q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">area</sup>t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bounce</sup>, where the sum is over all Schröder lattice paths, and area and bounce are simple statistics on these paths. For d=0, this reduces to Garsia and Haglund's formula for the q,t-Catalan sequence (2001). Our results build on symmetric function identities for sums of generalized Pieri coefficients and Macdonald polynomials due to Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler (1999) and Garsia and Haglund (2002). We also derive several transformation identities for sums of rational functions occurring in the theory of Macdonald polynomials and diagonal harmonics, and apply these to obtain a combinatorial formula for 〈∇e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−d</inf>h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>〉. We discuss how our formulas for 〈∇e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−d</inf>h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>〉 and 〈∇e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−d</inf>h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>〉 prove two special cases of a recent conjecture of Haglund, Haiman, Loehr, Remmel, and Ulyanov.

articleTitle: Fusion products, cohomology of GLN flag manifolds, and Kostka polynomials
abstract: We explain the relation between the fusion product of symmetric power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{sl}}_n$</tex> evaluation modules, as defined by Feigin and Loktev, and the graded coordinate ring R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</inf> which describes the cohomology ring of the flag variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{F}l_{\mu'}$</tex> of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>. The graded multiplicity spaces appearing in the decomposition of the fusion product into irreducible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{sl}}_n$</tex> -modules are identified with the multiplicity spaces of the Specht modules in R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</inf>. This proves that Kostka polynomials give the character of the fusion product in this case. In the case of the product of fundamental evaluation modules, we give the precise correspondence with the reduced wedge product, and thus the usual wedge space construction of irreducible level-1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\widehat{\text{sl}}}_n$</tex> -modules in the limit N → ∞. The multiplicity spaces are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W{({\text{sl}}_n)}$</tex> -algebra modules in this limit.

articleTitle: Weak Poincaré inequalities on path spaces
abstract: The weak Poincaré inequality is established on the finite time interval Brownian path space over a class of Riemannian manifolds with unbounded Ricci curvatures. Compatible, sufficient, and necessary curvature conditions are also presented for the inequality to hold on infinite time interval path spaces. Consequently, the convergence rates of the corresponding Ornstein-Uhlenbech semigroups are described.

articleTitle: On the bi-Hamiltonian structures of the Camassa-Holm and Harry Dym equations
abstract: We show that the bi-Hamiltonian structures of the Camassa-Holm and Harry Dym hierarchies can be obtained by applying a reduction process to a simple Poisson pair defined on the loop algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{sl}{(2,\mathbb{R})}$</tex> . The reduction process is a bi-Hamiltonian reduction that can be canonically performed on every bi-Hamiltonian manifold.

articleTitle: Chen Lie algebras
abstract: The Chen groups of a finitely presented group G are the lower central series quotients of its maximal metabelian quotient G/G″. The direct sum of the Chen groups is a graded Lie algebra, with bracket induced by the group commutator. If G is the fundamental group of a formal space, we give an analog of a basic result of Sullivan by showing that the rational Chen Lie algebra of G is isomorphic to the rational holonomy Lie algebra of G modulo the second derived subalgebra. Following an idea of Massey, we point out a connection between the Alexander invariant of a group G defined by commutator-relators and its integral holonomy Lie algebra. As an application, we determine the Chen Lie algebras of several classes of geometrically defined groups, including surface-like groups, fundamental groups of certain link complements in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and fundamental groups of complements of hyperplane arrangements in ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</sup>. For link groups, we sharpen Massey and Traldi's solution of the Murasugi conjecture. For arrangement groups, we prove that the rational Chen Lie algebra is combinatorially determined.

articleTitle: Asymptotic stability and completeness in the energy space for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with small solitary waves
abstract: We study a class of nonlinear Schrödinger equations which admit families of small solitary wave solutions. We consider solutions which are small in the energy space H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, and decompose them into solitary wave and dispersive wave components. The goal is to establish the asymptotic stability of the solitary wave and the asymptotic completeness of the dispersive wave. That is, we show that as t → ∞, the solitary wave component converges to a fixed solitary wave, and the dispersive component converges strongly in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> to a solution of the free Schrödinger equation.

articleTitle: The Cherednik kernel and generalized exponents
abstract: We show how the knowledge of the Fourier coefficients of the Cherednik kernel leads to combinatorial formulas for generalized exponents. We recover known formulas for generalized exponents of irreducible representations parameterized by dominant roots, and obtain new formulas for the generalized exponents for irreducible representations parameterized by the dominant elements of the root lattice which are sums of two orthogonal short roots.

articleTitle: A solution to Lipsman's conjecture for ℝ4
abstract: We consider the affine transformation of a nilpotent Lie group on ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. Lipsman (1995) conjectured that such an action is proper in the sense of Palais if and only if the action is compact isotropy (CI) in the sense of Kobayashi. This paper gives an affirmative solution to Lipsman's conjecture in the four-dimensional case.

articleTitle: Correlations between zeros of non-Gaussian random polynomials
abstract: The existence of the scaling limit and its universality for correlations between zeros of Gaussian random polynomials, or more generally, Gaussian random sections of powers of a line bundle over a compact manifold has been proved in a great generality in the works of Bogomolny, Bohigas, Lebœuf, Hannay, Bleher, Schiffman, Zelditch, and others. In the present work, we prove the existence of the scaling limit for a class of non-Gaussian random polynomials. Our main result is that away from the origin, the scaling limit exists and is universal so that it does not depend on the distribution of the coefficients. At the origin, the scaling limit is not universal, and we find a crossover from the nonuniversal asymptotics of the density of the probability distribution of zeros at the origin to the universal one away from the origin.

articleTitle: Combinatorial classes on ${\overline {\mathcal {M}}}_{g,n}$ are tautological
abstract: The combinatorial description via ribbon graphs of the moduli space of Riemann surfaces makes it possible to define combinatorial cycles in a natural way. Witten and Kontsevich first conjectured that these classes are polynomials in the tautological classes. We answer affirmatively to this conjecture and find recursively all the polynomials.

articleTitle: Q4: integrable master equation related to an elliptic curve
abstract: One of the most fascinating and technically demanding parts of the theory of two-dimensional integrable systems constitutes the models with the spectral parameter on an elliptic curve, including Landau-Lifshitz and Krichever-Novikov equations as well as elliptic Toda and Ruijsenaars-Toda lattices, elliptic Volterra lattice and Shabat-Yamilov lattice. We explain how all these models can be unified on the basis of a single equation Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> on a quad-graph. This discrete model plays the role of the “master equation” in the (sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> part of) 2D integrability: most of other models in this area can be obtained from this one by certain limiting procedures. More precisely, discrete versions of all of the above-mentioned models appear from Q4 imposed on a multidimensional cubic lattice. Zero-curvature representations for all models appear as a byproduct of the general construction.

articleTitle: A limiting absorption principle for the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation with Lp potentials
abstract: We obtain mapping estimates for the Schrödinger resolvent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-\Delta+V-\lambda^2)^{-1}$</tex> in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, where the potential is assumed to satisfy only an integrability condition. No pointwise decay or additional regularity is required. These results are closely related to Agmon's limiting absorption principle, and also to the Stein-Tomas theorem in Fourier analysis.

articleTitle: On a class of locally conformally flat manifolds
abstract: An important class of conformally flat structures are those derived from Kleinian groups. As an application of the Yamabe equation, Schoen and Yau (1986) proved that if M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>,g) is a smooth compact locally conformally flat manifold on which the Yamabe operator is positive, then the developing map of the holonomy cover of M is injective and the complement of its image in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> (the limit set) has Hausdorff dimension bounded by (n−2)/2. There are a family of fully nonlinear equations which prescribes the symmetric functions of the eigenvalues of the Weyl Schouten tensor A=(1/(n−2))(Rc−(R/(n−2))g), and a family of conformally covariant operators which prescribes higher-order curvature invariants. The positivity of such operators on a Kleinian group gives further control of the size of the limit set. In this paper, we carry out this analysis for the σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(A) equation as well as for the fourth-order Paneitz equation. In particular, under suitable additional bounds on the Ricci tensor, we show that the limit set has Hausdorff dimension bounded by (n−4)/2 if either of these two equations are positive. As a consequence, we extend the range of indices for which the homotopy groups vanish, that is, π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>(M)=0 for 2 ≤ i ≤ [n/2]+1.

articleTitle: Schubert varieties and the fusion products: The general case
abstract: This paper generalizes the results of our previous paper with B. Feigin to the case of the general <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{sl}}_2$</tex> Schubert varieties. We study the homomorphisms between different Schubert varieties and describe their geometry and the group of the line bundles. We also derive some consequences concerning the infinite-dimensional generalized affine Grassmannians.

articleTitle: Upper bound on the number of systems of Hecke eigenvalues for Siegel modular forms (mod p)
abstract: We derive an explicit upper bound for the number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{N}{(g,N,p)}$</tex> of systems of Hecke eigenvalues coming from Siegel modular forms mod p) of dimension g and level N relatively prime to p. In the special case of elliptic modular forms (g=1), our result agrees with recent work of G. Herrick.

articleTitle: On characterization of the range and inversion formulas for the geodesic X-ray transform
abstract: We describe a relation between the scattering relation, the Hilbert transform in frequency space, and the geodesic ray transform for simple, two-dimensional compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We use this relation to give a characterization of the range of the geodesic X-ray transform acting on scalar functions and vector fields in terms of the scattering relation which involves only measurements at the boundary. We also give inversion formulas for the geodesic X-ray transform acting on scalar functions and vector fields.

articleTitle: On integrals of Eisenstein series and derivatives of L-series
abstract: We give a simpler and more natural proof of a formula of Ahlgren, Berndt, Yee, and Zaharescu, which connects integrals of Eisenstein series, infinite products, and certain values of derivatives of Dirichlet L-series. Our approach shows that their result is a special case of a more general identity.

articleTitle: Zak transform, Weil representation, and integral operators with theta-kernels
abstract: The Weil representation of a real symplectic group Sp(2n, ℝ) admits a canonical extension to a holomorphic representation of a certain complex semigroup consisting of Lagrangian linear relations (this semigroup includes the Olshanskii semigroup). We obtain the explicit realization of the Weil representation of this semigroup in the Cartier model, that is, in the space of smooth sections of a certain line bundle on the 2n-dimensional torus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{T}^{2n}$</tex> . We show that operators of the representation are integral operators whose kernels are theta-functions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{T}^{4n}$</tex> . We also extend this construction to a functor from a certain category of Lagrangian linear relations between symplectic vector spaces of different dimensions to a category of integral operators acting on sections of line bundles on the tori.

articleTitle: The space of local fields as a module over the ring of local integrals of motion
abstract: The chiral space of local fields in sine-Gordon or the SU(2)-invariant Thirring model is studied as a module over the commutative algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D}$</tex> of local integrals of motion. Using the recent construction of form factors by means of quantum affine algebra at root of unity due to Feigin et al. we construct a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D}$</tex> -free Resolution of the space of local fields. In general, the cohomologies of the de Rham-type complex associated with the space of local fields are determined and shown to be the irreducible representations of the symplectic group Sp(2∞). Babelon-Bernard-Smirnov description of the space of local fields is automatically incorporated in this framework.

articleTitle: tt* geometry of rank two
abstract: A notion of a Frobenius manifold with a nice real structure was introduced by Hertling. It is called CDV structure (Cecotti-Dubrovin-Vafa structure). In this paper, we introduce a “positivity condition” on CDV structures and show that any Frobenius manifold of rank two with real dimension can be equipped with a positive CDV structure. We extend naturally the symmetries of Frobenius structures given by Dubrovin to symmetries of CDV structures, which will play an important role.

articleTitle: Hilbert schemes, integrable hierarchies, and Gromov-Witten theory
abstract: Various equivariant intersection numbers on Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane are computed, some of which are organized into τ-functions of 2-Toda hierarchies. A correspondence between the equivariant intersection on Hilbert schemes and stationary Gromov-Witten theory is established.

articleTitle: Hilbert's tenth problem for function fields of varieties over ℂ
abstract: Let K be the function field of a variety of dimension greater than or equal to 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Then Hilbert's tenth problem for K is undecidable. This generalizes the result by Kim and Roush, 1992, that Hilbert's tenth problem for the purely transcendental function field ℂ(t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is undecidable.

articleTitle: Ind-varieties of generalized flags as homogeneous spaces for classical ind-groups
abstract: The purpose of the present paper is twofold, to introduce the notion of a generalized flag in an infinite-dimensional vector space V (extending the notion of a flag of subspaces in a vector space) and to give a geometric realization of homogeneous spaces of the ind-groups SL(∞), SO(∞), and Sp(∞) in terms of generalized flags. Generalized flags in V are chains of subspaces which in general cannot be enumerated by integers. Given a basis E of V, we define a notion of E- commensurability for generalized flags, and prove that the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F\mathrm\ell{(\mathcal F,\mathrm E)}$</tex> of generalized flags E-commensurable with a fixed generalized flag <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal F$</tex> in V has a natural structure of an ind-variety. In the case when V is the standard representation of G = SL(∞), all homogeneous ind-spaces G/P for parabolic subgroups P containing a fixed splitting Cartan subgroup of G are of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}\ell{(\mathcal{F},E)}$</tex> . We also consider isotropic generalized flags. The corresponding ind-spaces are homogeneous spaces for SO(∞) and Sp(∞). As an application of the construction, we compute the Picard group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}\ell{(\mathcal{F},E)}$</tex> (and of its isotropic analogs) and show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}\ell{(\mathcal{F},E)}$</tex> is a projective ind-variety if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{F}$</tex> is a usual, possibly infinite flag of subspaces in V.

articleTitle: Minimality and nondegeneracy of degree-one Ginzburg-Landau vortex as a Hardy's type inequality
abstract: We consider the unique radially symmetric degree-one solution w(x) = U(r)e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iθ</sup> of the Ginzburg-Landau equation in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Δw+(1−∣w∣<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)w = 0, where ∣w(x)∣ → 1 as ∣x∣ → +∞. We provide an elementary proof of its locally minimizing character and nondegeneracy up to the obvious invariance of the equation in the natural Hilbert space for its second variation bilinear form. The proof reduces to an optimal vector-valued form of Hardy's inequality. As a consequence, we establish a Fredholm alternative in this space for the associated linearized operator.

articleTitle: Gaussian hypergeometric functions and traces of Hecke operators
abstract: We establish a simple inductive formula for the trace <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Tr}_k^\text new{(\Gamma_0{(8)},p)}$</tex> of the pth Hecke operator on the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_k^\text new{(\Gamma_0{(8)})}$</tex> of newforms of level 8 and weight k in terms of the values of <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-hypergeometric functions over the finite field F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>. Using this formula when k = 6, we prove a conjecture of Koike relating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Tr}_6^\text new{(\Gamma_0{(8)},p)}$</tex> to the values <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>(1)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> and <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(1)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>. Furthermore, we find new congruences between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Tr}_k^\text new{(\Gamma_0{(8)},p)}$</tex> and generalized Apéry numbers.

articleTitle: Vanishing of cohomology associated to quantized Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction
abstract: We prove a vanishing theorem of the cohomology arising from the two quantized Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions (“+” and “−” reductions) introduced by FeĬgin and Frenkel, and by Frenkel, Kac, and Wakimoto. As a consequence, the vanishing conjecture of Frenkel, Kac, and Wakimoto is proved for the “−” reduction and partially for the “+” reduction.

articleTitle: Periodic orbits for exact magnetic flows on surfaces
abstract: We show that any exact magnetic flow on a closed surface has periodic orbits in all energy levels. Moreover, we give homological and homotopical properties of these periodic orbits in terms of the Mañé's critical values of the corresponding Lagrangian. We also prove that if M is not the 2-torus, the energy level k is of contact type if and only if k > c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is Mañé's strict critical value. When M is the 2-torus, we give examples for which the energy level c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is of contact type.

articleTitle: Holomorphic discs, spin structures, and Floer cohomology of the Clifford torus
abstract: We compute the Bott-Morse Floer cohomology of the Clifford torus in ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> with all possible spin structures. Each spin structure is known to determine an orientation of the moduli space of holomorphic discs, and we analyze the change of orientation according to the change of spin structure of the Clifford torus. Also, we classify all holomorphic discs with boundary lying on the Clifford torus by establishing a Maslov index formula for such discs. As a result, we show that in odd dimensions, there exist two spin structures which give nonvanishing Floer cohomology of the Clifford torus, and in even dimensions, there is only one such spin structure. When the Floer cohomology is nonvanishing, it is isomorphic to the singular cohomology of the torus (with a Novikov ring as its coefficients). As a corollary, we prove that any Hamiltonian deformation of the Clifford torus intersects with it at least at 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> distinct intersection points when the intersection is transversal. We also compute the Floer cohomology of the Clifford torus with flat line bundles on it and verify the prediction made by Hori using a mirror symmetry calculation.

articleTitle: Bounded geodesics in moduli space
abstract: In the moduli space of quadratic differentials over complex structures on a surface, we construct a set of full Hausdorff dimension of points with bounded Teichmüller geodesic trajectories. The main tool is quantitative nondivergence of Teichmüller horocycles, due to Minsky and Weiss. This has an application to billiards in rational polygons.

articleTitle: On simple real lie bialgebras
abstract: The explicit list of all almost factorizable Lie bialgebra structures on real absolutely simple Lie algebras is given. By “absolutely simple” we mean a real Lie algebra whose complexification is simple.

articleTitle: A differential inequality for the isoperimetric profile
abstract: We show that the isoperimetric profile of a closed Riemannian manifold satisfies a second-order differential inequality which only depends on its dimension and on a lower bound on the Ricci curvature. Not only does this differential property enable us to derive regularity of the profile but it also provides a new proof of Lévy-Gromov inequality and leads to pinching theorems on the isoperimetric profile. Moreover, under a lower bound assumption on the Ricci curvature and on the Cheeger isoperimetric constant, we study the links between the convergence of the diameter, of the profile, and of the Cheeger isoperimetric constant.

articleTitle: A closer look at semistability for singular principal bundles
abstract: We substantially refine the theory of singular principal bundles introduced in a former paper. In particular, we show that we need only honest singular principal bundles in our compactification. These are objects which carry the structure of a rational principal bundle in the sense of Ramanathan. Moreover, we arrive at a much simpler semistability condition. In the case of a semisimple group, this is just the Gieseker version of Ramanathan's semistability condition for the corresponding rational principal G-bundle.

articleTitle: Grothendieck ring of pretriangulated categories
abstract: We consider the abelian group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PT}$</tex> generated by quasi-equivalence classes of pretriangulated DG categories with relations coming from semiorthogonal decompositions of corresponding triangulated categories. We introduce an operation of “multiplication” • on the collection of DG categories, which makes this abelian group into a commutative ring. A few applications are considered: representability of “standard” functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on smooth projective varieties and a construction of an interesting motivic measure.

articleTitle: The Chord problem and a new method of filling by pseudoholomorphic curves
abstract: Let M be a closed three-dimensional manifold with contact form λ so that Ker λ is tight. In this paper, we will present a first application of the filling method by pseudoholomorphic curves recently developed by the author. We will show that Legendrian knots L ⊂ M satisfying suitable assumptions admit a Reeb Chord, that is, there is a trajectory x(t) of the Reeb vector field and T > 0 such that x(0),x(T) ∈ L and x(0) ≠ x(T).

articleTitle: Representations of wreath products on cohomology of De Concini-Procesi compactifications
abstract: The wreath product W(r,n) of the cyclic group of order r and the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> acts on the corresponding projective hyperplane complement and on its wonderful compactification as defined by De Concini and Procesi. We give a formula for the characters of the representations of W(r,n) on the cohomology groups of this compactification, extending the result of Ginzburg and Kapranov in the r=1 case. As a corollary, we get a formula for the Betti numbers, which generalizes the result of Yuzvinsky in the r=2 case. Our method involves applying to the nested-set stratification a generalization of Joyal's theory of tensor species, which includes a link between polynomial functors and plethysm for general r. We also give a new proof of Lehrer's formula for the representations of W(r,n) on the cohomology groups of the hyperplane complement.

articleTitle: Well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the modified KdV equation with periodic boundary condition
abstract: We study the time local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the modified KdV equation on the one-dimensional torus. We prove that when 1/2 > s > 3/8, it is locally well posed in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>, but the uniformly continuous dependence of solution on initial data breaks down in contrast to the case s ≥ 1/2. This improves the result of Bourgain (1993).

articleTitle: New Lagrangian submanifolds of ℂℙn
abstract: We use Hamiltonian actions to construct new (as opposed to ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>) Lagrangian submanifolds of ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. First of all, a quotient of ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> by the dihedral group D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is a Lagrangian submanifold of ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Secondly, SU(n)/ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>/ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> are Lagrangian submanifolds of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{3}{8}\mathbb{P}^{\mathrm n^2-1}$</tex> .

articleTitle: On the distribution of modular symbols for compact surfaces
abstract: We prove that for all cocompact subgroups of SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℝ), the modular symbols appropriately normalized and ordered have an asymptotical normal distribution. In order to calculate the moments of the modular symbols, we introduce hyperbolic Eisenstein series.

articleTitle: Compactness for Yamabe metrics in low dimensions
abstract: We provide a detailed proof in low dimensions of a well-known result of Schoen: given a smooth compact Riemannian manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,g)$</tex> , the set of metrics conformal to g, with normalized constant scalar curvature, is precompact in the C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-topology.

articleTitle: Determining a semisimple group from its representation degrees
abstract: The Lie algebra of a compact semisimple Lie group G is determined by the degrees of the irreducible representations of G. However, two different groups can have the same representation degrees.

articleTitle: Shifted convolution sums and subconvexity bounds for automorphic L-functions
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f{(z)}=\sum a{(m)}m^{{(k-1)}/2}e{(mz)}\in S_k{(N,\chi_1)}$</tex> be a primitive cusp form of integral weight k, level N, and character χ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. For a smooth weight function g with compact support in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lbrack M_1,2M_1\rbrack}\times{\lbrack M_2,2M_2\rbrack}$</tex> and positive integers l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, h, the bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_{l_1m_1-l_2m_2=h}a{(m_1)}\overline{a{(m_2)}}g{(m_1,m_2)}1\ll_\varepsilon{(l_1M_1+l_2M_2)}^{1/2+\theta+\varepsilon}$</tex> with θ = 7/64 is shown. As an application, the shifted sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_{m\leq M}a{(m)}\overline{a{(m+h)}}$</tex> is bounded nontrivially for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h\ll M^{64/39-\varepsilon}$</tex> . Furthermore, the subconvexity bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_f{(1/2+it,\chi)}\ll_\varepsilon D^{71/167+\varepsilon}$</tex> for the L-function attached to the twist of f with a primitive character χ to modulus D is obtained.

articleTitle: A note on gaps of Hill's equation
abstract: We give new, short proofs of two facts relating the gap lengths of the spectrum of a potential q of Hill's equation, −y″ + qy = λ y, to its regularity. First, if the potential is in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>, then its weighted gap lengths, (n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, forman ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-sequence. Second, finite gap potentials are dense in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>.

articleTitle: Representation theory and quantum inverse scattering method: the open Toda chain and the hyperbolic Sutherland model
abstract: Using the representation theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gl}{(N)}$</tex> , we express the wave function of the GL(N,ℝ) Toda chain, which was recently obtained by two of us by the quantum inverse scattering method, in terms of multiple integrals. The main tool is our generalization of the Gelfand-Zetlin method to the case of infinite-dimensional representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gl}{(N)}$</tex> . The interpretation of this generalized construction in terms of the coadjoint orbits is given and the connection with the Yangian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gl}{(N)}$</tex> is discussed. We also give the hyperbolic Sutherland model eigenfunctions expressed in terms of integrals in the Gelfand-Zetlin representation. Using the example of the open Toda chain, we discuss the connection between the quantum inverse scattering method and representation theory.

articleTitle: Chern classes of birational varieties
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi:V\rightarrow W$</tex> be a birational map between smooth algebraic varieties in the same K-equivalence class. We prove that the total homology Chern classes of V and W are push-forwards of the same class from a resolution of indeterminacies of φ. For example, it follows that the push-forward of the total Chern class of a crepant resolution of a singular variety is independent of the resolution.

articleTitle: On the center of a compact group
abstract: We prove a recent conjecture due to Baumgärtel and Lledó according to which, for every compact group G, one has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{Z{(G)}}\approx C{(G)}$</tex> , where the “chain group” C(G) is the free abelian group (written multiplicatively) generated by the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{\mathrm G}$</tex> of isomorphism classes of irreducible representations of G modulo the relations [Z] = [X] · [Y] whenever Z is contained in X ⊗ Y. Thus the center Z(G) depends only on the (ordered) representation ring of G. Furthermore, we prove that every “t-map” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm\varphi:\widehat{\mathrm G}\rightarrow\mathrm A$</tex> into an abelian group, that is, every map satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm\varphi{(\mathrm Z)}=\mathrm\varphi{(\mathrm X)}\mathrm\varphi{(\mathrm Y)}$</tex> , whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm X,\mathrm Y,\mathrm Z\in\widehat{\mathrm G}$</tex> and Z ≺ X⊗ Y, factors through the restriction map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{\mathrm G}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathrm Z{(\mathrm G)}}$</tex> . All these results generalize to proreductive groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero.

articleTitle: Automorphisms and twisted loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebras
abstract: We describe the structure of the algebraic group of automorphisms of all simple finite-dimensional Lie superalgebras. Using this and étale cohomology considerations, we list all different isomorphism classes of the corresponding twisted loop superalgebras.

articleTitle: Orthogonal matrix polynomials satisfying second-order differential equations
abstract: We develop a general method that allows us to introduce families of orthogonal matrix polynomials of size N × N satisfying second-order differential equations. The presence of this extra property should make these orthogonal polynomials into useful tools in several areas of mathematics and its applications. Historically, this has certainly been the case for their scalar-valued versions. The subtlety of the noncommutative algebra of matrices can be exploited to yield many different such families, almost dwarfing the scalar situation by comparison. All these families form a nice and rich hierarchy starting from the classical Jacobi, Hermite, and Laguerre families, N=1, and increasing in number and variety as the size N increases. We illustrate the use of our method by giving large classes of generic examples of arbitrary size N.

articleTitle: An infinite-dimensional manifold structure for analytic Lie pseudogroups of infinite type
abstract: We construct an infinite-dimensional manifold structure adapted to analytic Lie pseudogroups of infinite type. More precisely, we prove that any isotropy subgroup of an analytic Lie pseudogroup of infinite type is a regular infinite-dimensional Lie group, modelled on a locally convex strict inductive limit of Banach spaces. This is an infinite-dimensional generalization to the case of Lie pseudogroups of the classical second fundamental theorem of Lie.

articleTitle: Exceptional Lie algebras with S4 structures over ℤ
abstract: We first give an alternative to Tits' second construction of the exceptional Lie algebras using the principle of triality. These algebras have a natural S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> action. We use the construction to obtain Lie algebras and algebraic groups over ℤ.

articleTitle: Invariant theory of GL(n) and intersection theory of Grassmannians
abstract: We give an algebro-geometric relation between intersection theory of Grassmannians and invariant theory of the general linear group. From points of intersection of Schubert varieties in Gr(r,n), we produce “all” invariants in tensor products of (associated) irreducible representations of SL(r).

articleTitle: Analysis of geometric stability
abstract: We identify the difference between the CM polarization and the Chow polarization on the “Hilbert scheme.” As a consequence, we give a numerical criterion for the CM stability as in Mumford's geometric invariant theory (GIT). Also, we write down an explicit formula for the generalized Futaki invariant in terms of weights and multiplicities of the associated degeneration.

articleTitle: Well-posedness results for the generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with arbitrary large initial data
abstract: We prove new local well-posedness results for the generalized Benjamin-Ono equation (GBO) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial_tu+\mathcal{H}\partial_x^2u+u^k\partial_xu=0$</tex> , k ≥ 2. By combining a gauge transformation with dispersive estimates, we establish the local well-posedness of GBO in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>(ℝ) for s ≥ 1/2 if k ≥ 5, s > 1/2 if k=2,4, and s≥ 3/4 if k=3. Moreover, we prove that in all these cases, the flow map is locally Lipschitz on H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>(ℝ).

articleTitle: The Navier-Stokes equations and the maximum principle
abstract: We consider the steady Navier-Stokes equations in a two-dimensional infinite channel with slip boundary conditions. Provided with a geometrical constraint on the domain, we are able to show existence of solutions for arbitrary large velocity data, including the flux of flow. The crucial point of the proof is the maximum principle for a reformulation of the problem. This technique gives a new type of estimates in the Hölder space for the solutions with the infinite Dirichlet integral.

articleTitle: Local pointwise estimates for solutions of the σ2 curvature equation on 4-manifolds
abstract: The study of the kth elementary symmetric function of the Weyl-Schouten curvature tensor of a Riemannian metric, the so called σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> curvature, has produced many fruitful results in conformal geometry in recent years, especially when the dimension of the underlying manifold is 3 or 4. In these studies in conformal geometry, the deforming conformal factor is considered to be a solution of a fully nonlinear elliptic PDE. Important advances have been made in recent years in the understanding of the analytic behavior of solutions of the PDE, including the adaptation of Bernstein-type estimates in integral form, global and local derivative estimates, classification of entire solutions, and analysis of blowing-up solutions. Most of these results require derivative bounds on the σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> curvature. The derivative estimates also require an a priori L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> bound on the solution. This work provides local L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> and Harnack estimates for solutions of the σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bounds on the σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> curvature, and the natural assumption of small volume (or total σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> curvature).

articleTitle: Connes' embedding problem and Lance's WEP
abstract: A II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-factor embeds into the ultraproduct of the hyperfinite II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-factor if and only if it satisfies the von Neumann algebraic analogue of Lance's weak expectation property (WEP). We give a self-contained proof of this fact.

articleTitle: Modular parametrizations of Neumann-Setzer elliptic curves
abstract: Suppose p is a prime of the form u<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 64 for some integer u, which we take to be 3 mod 4. Then there are two Neumann-Setzer elliptic curves E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of prime conductor p, and both have Mordell-Weil group ℤ/2ℤ. There is a surjective map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_0{(p)}\xrightarrow\pi E_0$</tex> that does not factor through any other elliptic curve (i.e., π is optimal), where X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(p) is the modular curve of level p. Our main result is that the degree of π is odd if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\equiv3{(\operatorname{mod}8)}$</tex> . We also prove the prime-conductor case of a conjecture of Glenn Stevens, namely that if E is an elliptic curve of prime conductor p, then the optimal quotient of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(p) in the isogeny class of E is the curve with minimal Faltings height. Finally we discuss some conjectures and data about modular degrees and orders of Shafarevich-Tate groups of Neumann-Setzer curves.

articleTitle: Uniform diameter bounds for some families of Cayley graphs
abstract: We prove that Cayley graphs of PSL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ/p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>ℤ) have uniform polylog diameter with respect to the natural projection of elements in PSL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ) generating a dense subgroup. The proof also provides a fast algorithm for finding a short path between two vertices.

articleTitle: Completely bounded maps into certain Hilbertian operator spaces
abstract: We prove a factorization of completely bounded maps from a C*-algebra A (or an exact operator space E ⊂ A) to ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> equipped with the operator space structure of (C,R)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> (0 < θ < 1) obtained by complex interpolation between the column and row Hilbert spaces. More precisely, if F denotes ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> equipped with the operator space structure of (C,R)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf>, then u: A → F is completely bounded if and only if there are states f, g on A and C > 0 such that for all a ∈ A, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Arrowvert ua\Arrowvert^2\leq Cf(a^\ast a)^{1-\theta}g(aa^\ast)^\theta$</tex> . This extends the case θ = 1/2 treated in a recent paper with Shlyakhtenko (2002). The constants we obtain tend to 1 when θ → 0 or θ→ 1, so that we recover, when θ = 0 (or θ = 1), the case of mappings into C (or into R), due to Effros and Ruan. We use analogs of “free Gaussian” families in nonsemifinite von Neumann algebras. As an application, we obtain that, if 0 < θ < 1, (C,R)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> does not embed completely isomorphically into the predual of a semifinite von Neumann algebra. Moreover, we characterize the subspaces S ⊂ R ⊕ C such that the dual operator space S* embeds (completely isomorphically) into M* for some semifinite von Neumann algebra M: the only possibilities are S = R, S = C, S = R ∩ C and direct sums built out of these three spaces. We also discuss when S ⊂ R ⊕ C is injective, and give a simpler proof of a result due to Oikhberg on this question. In the appendix, we present a proof of Junge's theorem that OH embeds completely isomorphically into a noncommutative L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-space. The main idea is similar to Junge's, but we base the argument on complex interpolation and Shlyakhtenko's generalized circular systems (or “generalized free Gaussian”), which somewhat unifies Junge's ideas with those of our work with Shlyakhtenko (2002).

articleTitle: Tensor fields and singular principal bundles
abstract: Let G be a complex reductive algebraic group. We construct the moduli spaces of tensor fields of special type on a large class of varieties X including seminormal varieties and varieties satisfying Serre's condition S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. We use them to construct compactified moduli spaces of principal G-bundles on X in case X is irreducible. We also give a simpler construction of the moduli spaces of orthogonal and symplectic sheaves on curves with ordinary nodes and cusps.

articleTitle: Janossy densities, multimatrix spacing distributions and Fredholm resolvents
abstract: A simple proof is given for a generalized form of a theorem of Soshnikov. The latter states that the Janossy densities for multilevel determinantal ensembles, supported on measurable subspaces of a set of measure spaces, are constructed by dualization of bases on dual pairs of N-dimensional function spaces with respect to a pairing given by integration on the complements of the given measurable subspaces. The generalization extends this to dualization with respect to measures modified by arbitrary sets of weight functions.

articleTitle: Points rationnels des variétés de Shimura
abstract: Soit X une variété algébrique projective définiesur un corps de nombres. Si X(ℂ) est hyperbolique, une conjecture de Lang prévoit que X(L) est fini pour tout corps de nombres L. Quand X est seulement quasi-projective et X(ℂ) hyperbolique on s'attend à un énoncé de finitude pour les points entiers de X(L) (qui est précisé dans le texte). Nous montrons ces énoncés de finitudes pour des variétés algébriques (variétés de Shimura) dont les points complexes sont des unions d'espaces localement symétriques hermitiens hyperboliques asssociés à des groupes algébriques sur ℚ de type classique. Ces variétés peuventêtre projectives, on obtient dans ce cas la finitude de X(L) pour tout corps de nombres L. Nous proposons et discutons aussi des conjectures concernant les points rationnels des variétés de Shimura. Let X be a projective algebraic variety defined over a number field. If X(ℂ) is hyperbolic, Lang's conjecture says that X(L) is finite for all number field L. When X is only quasi-projective and X(ℂ) is hyperbolic, one expects only that the integral points of X(L) is a finite set (a more precise expected statement is given in the text). We prove such a statement for some algebraic varieties X (Shimura varieties) such that X(ℂ) is a union of hyperbolic hermitian locally symmetric spaces associated to a ℚ-algebraic group of classical type. These varieties can be projective; in these cases X(L) is finite for all number field. We also propose and discuss several conjectures concerning rational points on Shimura varieties.

articleTitle: Bäcklund transformations of the sixth Painlevé equation in terms of Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
abstract: It is well known that the sixth Painlevé equation P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VI</inf> admits a group of Bäcklund transformations which is isomorphic to the affine Weyl group of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_4^{(1)}$</tex> . Although various aspects of this unexpectedly large symmetry have been discussed by many authors, there still remains a basic problem yet to be considered, that is, the problem of characterizing the Bäcklund transformations in terms of Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. In this direction, we show that the Bäcklund transformations are just the pullback of very simple transformations on the moduli of monodromy representations by the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. This result gives a natural and clear picture of the Bäcklund transformations.

articleTitle: The real locus of an involution map on the moduli space of flat connections on a Riemann surface
abstract: It is known that every nonorientable surface Σ has an orientable double cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde\Sigma$</tex> . The covering map induces an involution on the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$</tex> of gauge equivalence classes of flat G-connections on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde\Sigma$</tex> . We identify the relation between the moduli space<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}$</tex> and the fixed point set of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$</tex> . In particular, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}$</tex> is isomorphic to the fixed point set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$</tex> if and only if the order of the center of G is odd. One important application is that we give a way to construct a minimal Lagrangian submanifold of the moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$</tex> .

articleTitle: Singular ZN-curves and the Riemann-Hilbert problem
abstract: We are solving the classical Riemann-Hilbert problem of rank N > 1 on the extended complex plane punctured in 2m+2 points, for N × N quasi-permutation monodromy matrices. The Riemann-Hilbert problem is solved in terms of the Szegökernel of a certain Riemann surface branched over the given 2m+2 points. The monodromy group of this Riemann surface is determined from the quasi-permutation monodromy matrices of the Riemann-Hilbert problem by setting all its nonzero entries equal to one. In our case, the monodromy group of the Riemann surface turns out to be the cyclic subgroup Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> of the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>. This fact enables us to write the matrix entries of the solution of the N × N Riemann-Hilbert problem as a product of an algebraic function and θ-function quotients. The algebraic function is related to the Szegö kernel with zero characteristics. From the solution of the Riemann-Hilbert problem we automatically obtain a particular solution of the Schlesinger system. The τ-function of the Schlesinger system is computed explicitly in terms of θ-functions and the Bergmann projective connection of the Riemann surface. Finally, we study in detail the solution of the rank 3 problem with four singular points. In this case, the Riemann surface associated to the problem is a 2-sheeted cover of two elliptic curves which are 3-isogenous. As a result, the corresponding solution of the Riemann-Hilbert problem and the Schlesinger system is given in terms of Jacobi's ϑ-function.

articleTitle: Discrete invariants of varieties in positive characteristic
abstract: If S is a scheme of characteristic p, we define an F-zip over S to be a vector bundle with two filtrations plus a collection of semilinear isomorphisms between the graded pieces of the filtrations. For every smooth proper morphism X → S satisfying certain conditions, the de Rham bundles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{dR}^n{(X/S)}$</tex> have a natural structure of an F-zip. We givea complete classification of F-zips over an algebraically closed field by studying a semilinear variant of a variety that appears in recent work of Lusztig. For every F-zip over S, our methods give a scheme-theoretic stratification of S. If the F-zip is associated to an abelian scheme over S, the underlying topological stratification is the Ekedahl-Oort stratification. We conclude the paper with a discussion of several examples, such as good reductions of Shimura varieties of PEL type and K3 surfaces.

articleTitle: Real structures of models of arrangements
abstract: We will deal with two “hidden” real structures in the theory of models of subspace arrangements. Given a real subspace arrangement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and its complexification <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{A}}_\frac{3}{8}$</tex> , the first structure is a real De Concini-Procesi model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde{Y}_{A}$</tex> that can be seen as the manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{Re}Y_{{\text{A}}_{\frac{3}{8}}}$</tex> of (canonical) real points inside the complex De Concini-Procesi model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y_{{\text{A}}_\frac{3}{8}}$</tex> . We will study its combinatorial properties by describing it as a quotient of a real model with corners <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CY_\text A$</tex> introduced in 2003. A second structure arises, on the contrary, as an “extension” of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CY_\text A$</tex> , when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is a Coxeter arrangement. We will “add faces” to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CY_\text A$</tex> and obtain a convex body (or even a polytope); this gives rise to an interesting new family of “realized” posets which includes for instance Kapranov's permutoassociahedra.

articleTitle: When the Morse index is infinite
abstract: Let f be a smooth Morse function on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert manifold, all of whose critical points have infinite Morse index and coindex. For any critical point x, choose an integer a(x arbitrarily. Then there exists a Riemannian structure on M such that the corresponding gradient flow of f has the following property: for any pair of critical points x,y, the unstable manifold of x and the stable manifold of y have a transverse intersection of dimension a(x)−a(y.

articleTitle: Infinite comatrix corings
abstract: We characterize the corings whose category of comodules has a generating set of small projective comodules in terms of the (noncommutative) descent theory. In order to extricate the structure of these corings, we give a generalization of the notions of comatrix coring and Galois comodule which avoid finiteness conditions. A sufficient condition for a coring to be isomorphic to an infinite comatrix coring is found. We deduce in particular that any coalgebra over a field and the coring associated to a group-graded ring are isomorphic to adequate infinite comatrix corings. We also characterize when the free module canonically associated to a (not necessarily finite) set of group-like elements is Galois.

articleTitle: Zéro-cycles de degré un sur les espaces homogènes
abstract: We explain how to build homogeneous spaces of a connected linear algebraic group, having zero-cycles of degree one but no rational point, even on a smooth compactification. Thus, we give a negative answer to a recent question asked by Burt Totaro. Roughly speaking, the strategy is as follows: we apply a nonabelian cohomological machinery to some extension of finite groups, which is non-split, but split over every p-Sylow of the base. We give two precise examples: the first and easiest one, over the field ℂ((x))((y)); the second one, which requires a little more work, over a local or global field, and with finite abelian stabilizers. Both are rational varieties.

articleTitle: Renormalization and motivic Galois theory
abstract: We investigate the nature of divergences in quantum field theory, showing that they are organized in the structure of a certain “motivic Galois group” U*, which is uniquely determined and universal with respect to the set of physical theories. The renormalization group can be identified canonically with a one-parameter subgroup of U*. The group U* arises through a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Its representations classify equisingular flat vector bundles, where the equisingularity condition is a geometric formulation of the fact that in quantum field theory the counterterms are independent of the choice of a unit of mass. As an algebraic group scheme, U* is a semidirect product by the multiplicative group<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}_m$</tex> of a prounipotent group scheme whose Lie algebra is freely generated by one generator in each positive integer degree. There is a universal singular frame in which all divergences disappear. When computed as iterated integrals, its coefficients are certain rational numbers that appear in the local index formula of Connes-Moscovici. When working with formal Laurent series over ℚ, the data of equisingular flat vector bundles define a Tannakian category whose properties are reminiscent of a category of mixed Tate motives.

articleTitle: Affine lie group approach to a derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation and its similarity reduction
abstract: A generalization of the Drinfel'd-Sokolov hierarchies is proposed using the framework of Sato-Wilson dressing method. In the case of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_1^{(1)}$</tex> -type affine Lie group, we obtain the hierarchy that includes the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation. We give two types of affine Weyl group symmetry of the hierarchy based on the Gauss decomposition. The fourth Painlevé equation and its Weyl group symmetry are obtained as a similarity reduction. We also discuss the connection between the reduced system and monodromy-preserving deformations.

articleTitle: Equations of Shimura curves of genus two
abstract: We present explicit models for Shimura curves X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> of genus two and their Atkin-Lehner quotients X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>/〈 ω <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> 〉. We show that several equations conjectured by Kurihara are correct and compute for them the kernel of Ribet's isogeny J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">new</sup> → J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> between the new part of the Jacobian of the modular curve X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(D) and the Jacobian of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>.

articleTitle: Quasideterminants and Casimir elements for the general linear Lie superalgebra
abstract: We apply the techniques of quasideterminants to construct new families of Casimir elements for the general linear Lie superalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gl}{({m\vert n})}$</tex> whose images under the Harish-Chandra isomorphism are the elementary, complete, and power sums supersymmetric functions, respectively.

articleTitle: Rigidity for quasi-Fuchsian actions on negatively curved spaces
abstract: We prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G\curvearrowright X$</tex> is a convex cocompact isometric group action on a CAT(−1) space, and the limit set has Hausdorff and topological dimensions equal to 1, then the action preserves a convex subset Y⊆X isometric to ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This implies a conjecture by M. Bourdon. Our methods also yield a new proof of the n-dimensional analog of this statement for n≥<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: The Arnold-Givental conjecture and moment Floer homology
abstract: We prove the Arnold-Givental conjecture for a class of Lagrangian submanifolds in Marsden-Weinstein quotients which are fixed point sets of an antisymplectic involution. For these Lagrangians, the Floer homology cannot in general be defined by standard means due to the bubbling phenomenon. To overcome this difficulty, we consider moment Floer homology whose boundary operator is defined by counting solutions of the symplectic vortex equations on the strip. The moduli space of these solutions has better compactness properties than the moduli space of the original Floer equations.

articleTitle: Stacks of quantization-deformation modules on complex symplectic manifolds
abstract: On a complex symplectic manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> , we construct the stack of quantization-deformation modules, that is, (twisted) modules of microdifferential operators with an extra central parameter τ, a substitute to the lack of homogeneity. We also quantize involutive submanifolds of contact manifolds.

articleTitle: From double affine Hecke algebras to quantized affine Schur algebras
abstract: We prove an equivalence between some category of modules of the double affine Hecke algebra of type A and another of the quantized affine Schur algebra.

articleTitle: Free analysis questions I: duality transform for the coalgebra of ∂X:B
abstract: We construct a duality transform for the coalgebra of the free difference quotient derivation-comultiplication of an operator with respect to a free algebra of scalars. The dual object is realized in an algebra of matricial analytic functions endowed with yet another generalization of the difference quotient derivation.

articleTitle: Hecke operators on period functions for the full modular group
abstract: Matrix representations of Hecke operators on classical holomorphic cusp forms and corresponding period polynomials are well known. In this paper we define Hecke operators on period functions introduced recently by Lewis and Zagier and show how they are related to the Hecke operators on Maass cusp forms. Moreover, we give an explicit general compatibility criterion for formal sums of matrices to represent Hecke operators on period functions. An explicit example of such matrices with only nonnegative entries is constructed.

articleTitle: Hyperbolic volume of representations of fundamental groups of cusped 3-manifolds
abstract: Let W be a compact manifold and let ρ be a representation of its fundamental group into PSL(2, C). Then the volume of ρ is defined by taking any ρ-equivariant map from the universal cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{W}$</tex> to ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and then by integrating the pullback of the hyperbolic volume form on a fundamental domain. It turns out that such a volume does not depend on the choice of the equivariant map. Dunfield extended this construction to the case of a noncompact (cusped) manifold M, but he did not prove that the volume is well defined in all cases. We prove here that the volume of a representation is always well defined and depends only on the representation. Moreover, we show that this volume can be easily computed by straightening any ideal triangulation of M. We show that the volume of a representation is bounded from above by the relative simplicial volume of M. Finally, we prove a rigidity theorem for representations of the fundamental group of a hyperbolic manifold. Namely, we prove that if M is hyperbolic and vol(ρ) = vol(M), then ρ is discrete and faithful.

articleTitle: Configuration spaces and Massey products
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study and compare the collapsing of two spectral sequences converging to the cohomology of a configuration space. The noncollapsing of these spectral sequences is related, in some cases, to the existence of Massey products in the cohomology of the manifold M.

articleTitle: On the local Severi problem
abstract: For a given singularity of a plane curve, we consider the locus of nodal deformations of the singularity with the given number of nodes and describe possible components of the locus. An application to the symplectic isotopy problem is presented.

articleTitle: Multivariable Rankin-Selberg integrals for orthogonal groups
abstract: We show a relation between a certain period and the existence of a simple pole for the spin and standard partial L functions corresponding to a generic cuspidal representation defined on the group GSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>(A). We also relate these two conditions with the functorial lift from the exceptional group G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to GSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>.
