The main new ingridient is a new multivariable Rankin-Selberg integral which represents the above two L functions.

articleTitle: On the distribution of lattice points in thin annuli
abstract: We show that the number of lattice points lying in a thin annulus has a Gaussian value distribution if the width of the annulus tends to zero sufficiently slowly as we increase the inner radius.

articleTitle: Global boundedness for decorated sheaves
abstract: An important classification problem in algebraic geometry deals with pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal{E} ,\varphi)$</tex> , consisting of a torsion-free sheaf <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{E}$</tex> and a nontrivial homomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi:{(\mathcal{E}^{\otimes a})}^{\otimes b}\rightarrow\operatorname{det}{(\mathcal{E})}^{\otimes c}\otimes \mathcal{L}$</tex> on a polarized complex projective manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,{\text{O}}_X{(1)})$</tex> , the input data a, b, c, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}$</tex> as well as the Hilbert polynomial of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{E}$</tex> being fixed. The solution to the classification problem consists of a family of moduli spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}^\delta:=\mathcal{M}_{a/b/c/L/P}^{\delta-ss}$</tex> for the δ-semistable objects, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta\in \mathbb{Q}{\lbrack x\rbrack}$</tex> can be any positive polynomial of degree at most dim X−1. In this paper, we show that there are only finitely many distinct moduli spaces among the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M}^\delta$</tex> and that they sit in a chain of “GIT-flips.” This property has been known and proved by ad hoc arguments in several special cases. In our paper, we apply refined information on the instability flag to solve this problem. This strategy is inspired by the fundamental paper of Ramanan and Ramanathan on the instability flag.

articleTitle: Mirković-Vilonen cycles and polytopes in type A
abstract: We study, in type A, the algebraic cycles (MV-cycles) discovered by Mirković and Vilonen. In particular, we partition the loop Grassmannian into smooth pieces such that the MV-cycles are their closures. We explicitly describe the points in each piece using the lattice model of the loop Grassmannian in type A. The partition is invariant under the action of the coweights and, up to this action, the pieces are parametrized by the Kostant parameter set. This description of MV-cycles allows us to prove the main result of the paper: the computation of the moment map images of the MV-cycles (MV-polytopes) by identifying the vertices of each polytope.

articleTitle: Combinatorial consequences of Arthur's conjectures and the Burger-Sarnak method
abstract: The Burger-Sarnak principle states that the restriction to a reductive subgroup of an automorphic representation of a reductive group has automorphic support. Arthur's conjectures parametrize automorphic representations by means of the (Langlands) dual group. Taken together, these principles, combined with some new arguments, imply that unipotent orbits in a Langlands dual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat G$</tex> behave functorially with respect to arbitrary morphisms H → G of semisimple groups. The existence of this functoriality is proved for SL(n), and combinatorial descriptions of it (due to Kazhdan, Venkatesh, and Waldspurger) are proposed.
